docs.title: Cattle & Buffalo Breed Classifier
docs.text:
A lightweight, mobile-deployable image classifier for 50 Indian cattle breeds and 18 Indian buffalo breeds. Built on EfficientNet-Lite with CBAM/SE attention and a 3-head multi-task training pipeline, with a React web app, a Flask API and an on-device OOD safety layer.

Field Value Breeds 50 cattle + 18 buffalo = 68 total Backbone EfficientNet-Lite2 (~6M params) or Lite4 (~13M params) Input 260 × 260 RGB Training 2-phase: head warm-up → multi-task fine-tune (+ EMA, optional teacher distillation; QAT opt-in) Export TFLite INT8, ONNX Runtime INT8, ONNX, FP16, Portable bundle Dataset Kaggle: algsoch/breed-cattle-buffalo Web app React 18 + Vite (breed-classifier-react/) — zero-crop 260×260 capture, advanced optimizer panel, herd session, bilingual EN/தமிழ் Serving Flask REST API + Socket.IO (server/), standalone tester (test_model.py) Safety Post-hoc energy/MSP OOD detector with per-model calibration (including manual folder recalibration)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:

cd ML-CB-B-identifier

docs.title: 15. Android Deployment
docs.text: The Android pipeline targets two runtimes — TFLite (what the Flutter app uses today via tflite_flutter) and ONNX Runtime Mobile. Mobile INT8 comes from converter-side PTQ, not PyTorch QAT.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
data/raw → src.train (2 phases, EMA, optional --teacher distillation)
        → outputs/checkpoints/<backbone>_phase2_best_<runid>.pt   (EMA weights)
        → src.export --mode tflite | onnx-int8            (INT8 PTQ)
        → flutter_app/assets/models/{model.tflite, labels_*.txt}
        → src.parity_check                                (accuracy gate)

docs.title: Step 1 — Train
docs.text:
Default training is 2 phases (head warmup → multi-task fine-tune with EMA). For maximum accuracy, distill from a lite4 teacher:

# Teacher (once): lite4 + CBAM
python -m src.train --backbone lite4

# Student: same lite2 size/latency, teacher-quality logits
python -m src.train --backbone lite2 \
  --teacher outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt

docs.title: Step 2 — Export
docs.text:
# TFLite INT8 — full-integer PTQ, calibrated on ~500 real train images.
# Copies model.tflite + labels into flutter_app/assets/models/ automatically.
python -m src.export --mode tflite --backbone lite2

# ONNX Runtime Mobile INT8 — QDQ static quantization, per-channel weights.
python -m src.export --mode onnx-int8 --backbone lite2

TFLite toolchain (only needed for --mode tflite):

pip install tensorflow onnx2tf tf-keras onnx-graphsurgeon sng4onnx onnxsim

docs.title: Step 3 — Parity Gate
docs.text:
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 \
  --tflite outputs/export/lite2_int8.tflite \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx \
  --split val

Acceptance: INT8 within 1 pt combined_top1 of fp32. If it fails, ship the FP32 TFLite fallback (<backbone>_fp32.tflite, emitted alongside) or revisit calibration.

docs.title: On-device Input Convention
docs.text:
Mobile artifacts have ImageNet normalization baked into the graph:

Value Input RGB float32 in [0, 1], shape [1, 3, 260, 260] (static batch 1) Preprocessing on device pixel / 255.0 — exactly what the Flutter engine already does Outputs binary [1,2], cattle [1,57], buffalo [1,18] logits, read by index 0/1/2 Post-processing softmax + argmax, species-gated breed head (as in the app)

docs.title: Artifacts in the App
docs.text:
flutter_app/assets/models/
├── model.tflite            # INT8 compute, float32 [0,1] I/O
├── labels_binary.txt       # "cattle" (index 0) / "buffalo" (index 1)
├── labels_cattle.txt       # 57 lines, line i = class i
└── labels_buffalo.txt      # 18 lines, line i = class i

docs.title: Model Sizes (measured, lite2)
docs.text: Artifact Size ONNX FP32 (reference) ~25.7 MB ONNX INT8 (QDQ, mobile) ~7.1 MB TFLite INT8 ~6–7 MB (expected)

docs.title: QAT — optional recovery path only
docs.text: python -m src.train --include-qat (OFF by default) fine-tunes with per-tensor fake-quantization observers (the x86 per-channel default broke conversion), starting from the best phase-2 EMA checkpoint, and saves a timestamped <backbone>_quantized_<runid>.pt. Use it only if converter PTQ drops more than ~2 pts — the artifact is not a TFLite/ORT model. (src.export._sanitize_state_dict can strip the QAT/fused keys and re-load it as a float model, but exporting the phase-2 EMA checkpoint is still preferred.)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Complete command-line flag reference for all tools in the Cattle & Buffalo Breed Classifier project.

docs.title: python local_train.py — Automated Pipeline
docs.text:
The fully automated 8-stage pipeline: prerequisites → venv → dataset → verify → train → export.

python local_train.py [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Data Mode (mutually exclusive — pick at most one)
docs.text:
Flag Description --half-data Use 50% of images per breed (deterministic, seed=42) --quarter-data Use 25% of images per breed (deterministic, seed=42) --smoke-test Use 5 images per breed, 1 epoch per phase (seconds) --full-data Explicitly use all images (same as default, makes intent clear) (none) Use all images (default)

All subset modes maintain the full 57-cattle / 18-buffalo class map. The model architecture is identical across all modes.

docs.title: Model Configuration
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --backbone lite2 | lite4 lite2 Backbone architecture (~6M vs ~13M params) --attention cbam | se cbam Attention module type

docs.title: Training Overrides
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --include-qat flag off Enable the optional Phase 3 (QAT) — a recovery tool; mobile INT8 comes from converter PTQ (Android Deployment) --phase1-epochs int 8 Override Phase 1 epoch count (all-heads warmup) --phase2-epochs int 80 Override Phase 2 epoch count (multi-task fine-tune) --phase3-epochs int 10 Override Phase 3 epoch count (QAT) --num-workers int 4 DataLoader worker process count

docs.title: Skip Stages
docs.text: Flag Description --skip-download Skip Kaggle dataset download — data already in data/raw/ --skip-setup Skip .venv creation and dependency install --skip-verify Skip architecture verification (src.verify) --skip-export Skip multi-format model export after training

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Fastest local run
python local_train.py --quarter-data

# Half data, include QAT for Android
python local_train.py --half-data --include-qat

# Full data, lite4 backbone (teacher run for distillation)
python local_train.py --backbone lite4

# Re-run training only (skip setup + download)
python local_train.py --half-data --skip-setup --skip-download

# Smoke test — verifies the full pipeline in seconds
python local_train.py --smoke-test

docs.title: python -m src.train — Core Training Engine
docs.text:
Runs the 3-phase training loop directly. local_train.py wraps this with automated setup and export stages.

python -m src.train [OPTIONS]

Run from the project root directory (not inside src/).

docs.title: Model Configuration
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --backbone lite2 | lite4 lite2 Backbone architecture --weights path project root .pth Custom pretrained .pth weights path --attention cbam | se cbam Attention module type

docs.title: Data & I/O
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --data path data/raw/ Raw image root directory --split-dir path data/splits/ CSV split output directory --export-dir path outputs/export/portable/ Portable export destination directory

docs.title: Device & Workers
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --batch-size int 64 Per-GPU batch size (auto-scaled by local_train.py) --num-workers int 4 DataLoader worker processes --device str auto Force device: cuda or cpu (auto-detects by default) --seed int 42 Global random seed

docs.title: Hyperparameters
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --weight-decay float 1e-2 AdamW weight decay --label-smoothing float 0.1 Label smoothing factor (prevents overconfident predictions) --warmup-epochs int 3 Linear LR warmup epochs (Phase 2 only) --grad-accum int 2 Gradient accumulation steps (effective_batch = batch_size × grad_accum)

docs.title: Phase Control
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --phase1-epochs int 8 Phase 1 epochs (all-heads warmup) --phase2-epochs int 80 Phase 2 epochs (multi-task fine-tune + EMA) --phase3-epochs int 10 Phase 3 epochs (QAT, opt-in) --include-qat flag off Enable Phase 3 (QAT). Mobile INT8 comes from converter PTQ instead — see Export & Deployment --skip-qat flag off Kept for backwards compatibility; QAT is already off by default

docs.title: Distillation
docs.text:
Flag Type Default Description --teacher path off Teacher checkpoint (.pt) for knowledge distillation, e.g. outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt --teacher-backbone lite2 | lite4 lite4 Teacher backbone architecture --teacher-attention cbam | se same as student Teacher attention type

Blend and temperature are configured in src/config.py (KD_ALPHA=0.7, KD_TEMPERATURE=4.0).

docs.title: Data Mode (mutually exclusive)
docs.text: Flag Description --smoke-test 5 images/breed, 1 epoch per phase (real data, not random batches) --half-data 50% of images per breed, same 70/15/15 stratified split --quarter-data 25% of images per breed, same 70/15/15 stratified split (none) Full dataset (default)

docs.title: Augmentation (ALL OFF by default — opt-in per run)
docs.text: Flag Description --mix Enable CutMix/MixUp (same-species pairing, α=0.4/0.2, p=0.25) --flip Enable RandomHorizontalFlip --color-jitter Enable ColorJitter --randaugment Enable RandAugment(ops=2, mag=5) --rrc Enable RandomResizedCrop(260, scale=0.8–1.0) --augment-all Enable flip + color-jitter + randaugment + rrc + mix --no-mix Force-disable mixing (default)

docs.title: Imbalance & Output
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --logit-adjust flag off Enable logit adjustment on top of the sampler (off by default; double-corrects) --logit-adjust-prior sampled | raw sampled Prior source when logit adjustment is enabled --rare-threshold int 30 Breeds below this many train images are excluded from CutMix/MixUp --contrastive-weight float 0.2 SupCon weight (0 disables) --run-tag str auto DD-MM-YYYY-HH-MM Run id for timestamped outputs

docs.title: Compilation
docs.text: Flag Description --no-compile Disable torch.compile (auto-set on Windows; use to debug on Linux too) --no-export Skip automatic portable export after training completes

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Sanity check — full pipeline in seconds
python -m src.train --smoke-test

# Quarter-data training (recommended for local GPU)
python -m src.train --quarter-data

# Half-data with overridden epochs
python -m src.train --half-data --phase2-epochs 20

# Full training with lite4 backbone (teacher run)
python -m src.train --backbone lite4

# Full training, distilled from the lite4 teacher
python -m src.train --backbone lite2 \
  --teacher outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt

# Opt-in QAT phase (recovery path; mobile INT8 uses converter PTQ)
python -m src.train --backbone lite2 --include-qat

# Override hyperparameters explicitly
python -m src.train \
  --backbone lite4 \
  --batch-size 32 \
  --phase1-epochs 8 \
  --phase2-epochs 80 \
  --weight-decay 0.01 \
  --label-smoothing 0.05 \
  --device cuda

# CPU-only run (no torch.compile)
python -m src.train --quarter-data --device cpu --no-compile

docs.title: python -m src.export — Model Export
docs.text:
Exports a trained checkpoint to desktop or mobile formats.

python -m src.export [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --backbone lite2 | lite4 lite2 Which backbone's checkpoint to load --mode onnx | onnx-int8 | tflite | float16 | portable required Export format --checkpoint path auto (<backbone>_phase2_best_<runid>.pt) Specific .pt file to export --calibration-images int 500 Train images used for INT8 calibration (tflite / onnx-int8) --skip-app-assets flag off Don't copy TFLite artifacts into flutter_app/assets/models/ --onnx-static-batch flag off Fix batch size 1 in the fp32 ONNX export

docs.title: Export Modes
docs.text:
Mode Output File Description portable outputs/export/portable/<backbone>_<tag>/ Self-contained folder: model.pt + class JSONs + metadata. Requires BreedClassifier class to load. onnx outputs/export/<backbone>_fp32.onnx ONNX opset 13; caller-normalized input (test_model.py compatible) tflite <backbone>_fp32.tflite + <backbone>_int8.tflite + labels_*.txt Full-integer INT8 PTQ via onnx2tf; input [0,1], normalization baked in; auto-copies into flutter_app/assets/models/ onnx-int8 outputs/export/<backbone>_mobile_int8.onnx QDQ static INT8 for ONNX Runtime Mobile; per-channel weights, calibrated on real train images float16 outputs/export/<backbone>_float16.pt FP16 TorchScript

--mode int8 (x86 PTQ) was removed — it failed conversion and its artifacts were unusable on Android. Running it prints guidance to use tflite / onnx-int8.

# Desktop testing formats

python -m src.export --mode onnx --backbone lite2

docs.title: python -m src.parity_check — Export Parity Gate
docs.text:
Compares the fp32 PyTorch reference against the mobile artifacts on the same data — the accuracy gate every export must pass.

python -m src.parity_check [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Type Default Description --checkpoint path auto (<backbone>_phase2_best_<runid>.pt) fp32 reference checkpoint --backbone lite2 | lite4 lite2 Reference backbone --tflite path — TFLite artifact (fp32 or INT8) --onnx-int8 path — Quantized ONNX (mobile convention: input [0,1]) --onnx path — fp32 ONNX (caller-normalized convention) --split val | test val Split to evaluate --limit int 0 (all) Max images per runtime --synthetic int 0 Skip the dataset; compare N random inputs (max |Δlogit|) --tolerance float 0.01 Allowed combined_top1 drop vs fp32 --out path outputs/metrics/<backbone>_parity*.json JSON report path

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Accuracy table: binary_acc, cattle_acc, buffalo_acc, combined_top1, combined_top3 per runtime
  • Deltas vs pytorch_fp32 and a PASS / FAIL verdict against the tolerance
  • Synthetic mode: per-head max |Δlogit| (guidance < 0.05)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Full accuracy parity on the validation split
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 \
  --tflite outputs/export/lite2_int8.tflite \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx \
  --split val

# Quick artifact-only check without any dataset
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 --synthetic 16 \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx

docs.title: Inference Flow
docs.text:
Image → Resize(260) → CenterCrop(260) → ToTensor()
     → model.forward() → {binary, cattle, buffalo, features, embedding, traits}
     → Energy OOD check (abort if OOD)
     → soft routing: p(species)·softmax(head) over all 68 breeds → top-k

docs.title: Client Capture Flow (React, zero-crop)
docs.text:
The web client normalises every input to the model input size before upload, so the server-side Resize(260) → CenterCrop(260) becomes an identity pass-through and no part of the animal is discarded:

Original image (EXIF applied)
  → 260×260 canvas: stretch (default) | pad · ImageNet mean | pad · ambient blur | pad · black
  → optional 1:1 manual framing (pan on both axes) applied to the ORIGINAL
  → POST /api/predict (260×260 JPEG + original filename)
  → ResultWorkspace (Big-4 species / breed / gender / age, read-only)
  → quality gate + OOD explainer (blur/exposure/framing, trilingual tips)
  → Farmer advisory / breed encyclopedia tabs + printable report card
  → herd session log → CSV / JSON / ODT export

See Web Application for the full client architecture and Manual OOD calibration for the folder-based threshold workflow.

docs.title: Post-hoc Attributes — Gender, Age Group & Morphological Traits
docs.text:
Five outputs from one existing checkpoint, with no retraining:

# Output Source Confidence 1 Species (Cattle / Buffalo) BreedClassifier.binary_head species_confidence 2 Breed Top-1 / Top-5 cattle_head / buffalo_head (soft routing) top_breed_confidence, top5_breeds[].confidence 3 Gender CLIP zero-shot, else morphological heuristic gender.confidence 4 Age group CLIP zero-shot, else morphological heuristic age_group.confidence 5 Traits (hump, horn, coat, ear, dewlap, face, size) trait_heads already inside the checkpoint traits_detail[].confidence

The checkpoint is lite2_phase2_best_v26_1012-2332_f9ce.pt (or any checkpoint that contains trait_heads.* tensors). ONNX exports keep working unchanged.

docs.title: 1. Whole-animal preprocessing
docs.text:
Training-eval used shortest-side resize + CenterCrop(260). On a 4:3 phone photo that discards ~25% of the width — the strip that carries horns, udder and tail. Inference now uses PadToSquare(260) (long side → 260, short side padded with the ImageNet mean, which becomes ≈0 after normalization), so the whole body profile reaches the network.

Implemented once in src/preprocess.py and used by both entry points (test_model.py, server/services/inference.py); src/data_pipeline.py re-exports the same class as _PadToSquare so training and inference cannot drift.

# default: keep the whole frame
python run.py

# legacy parity with the exported ONNX/Flutter preprocessor
BREEDID_PAD_TO_SQUARE=0 python run.py

Toggle: src/config.py → INFERENCE_PAD_TO_SQUARE (env override above).

Expect slightly different — not necessarily worse — probabilities on crops where the animal already filled the centre: the network now also sees the padded border. Compare both settings with scripts/verify_attributes.py and your own validation images before shipping.

docs.title: 2. Trait heads (already trained, now exposed)
docs.text:
src/train.py attaches a TraitClassifier only while --trait-weight > 0, and src/export.py excludes it from the exported graph — but the trained tensors remain in the .pt file:

trait_heads.heads.{hump,horn,coat,ear,dewlap,face,size}.0.{weight,bias}   # Linear(1280, 256)
trait_heads.heads.{...}.3.{weight,bias}                                    # Linear(256, N_field)

On load, src.model.attach_trait_heads():

  1. reads each field's in_dim, hidden_dim and out_dim from the checkpoint tensors (no hardcoded widths),
  2. rebuilds a TraitClassifier with exactly those shapes,
  3. loads every trait_heads.* tensor,
  4. stores the module as model.trait_heads and keeps the vocab/metadata in model.trait_heads.trait_meta.

During predict(), the pooled 1280-d feature vector is passed to those heads (src.model.predict_traits), and src.attributes_zeroshot.decode_traits() turns the argmax indices into display strings using data/breed_traits.json — the same sorted vocabulary build_trait_vocab() produced at training time.

Vocabulary drift guard. If data/breed_traits.json gains/loses values so a field's vocabulary length no longer matches the checkpoint's out_dim, that field falls back to opaque class_<i> labels rather than silently mapping an index to the wrong trait. traits_meta.source reports breed_traits.json / partial_fallback / fallback.

Missing JSON. TRAIT_GENERIC_LABELS in src/attributes_zeroshot.py provides ordered human labels (Hump: Absent/Small/Medium/Large/…, Dewlap: Minimal/Moderate/Large & Pendulous, Size: Small/Compact → Large).

ONNX models do not expose pooled features, so traits is {} and traits_meta.reason = "onnx"; gender/age still work from the heuristic.

docs.title: 3. Gender & age estimation (src/attributes_zeroshot.py)
docs.text: Runs after the breed decision and only when is_ood == False.

docs.title: Engine A — CLIP zero-shot (primary)
docs.text:
• Lazy-loads openai/clip-vit-base-patch32 through transformers (CLIPProcessor, CLIPModel), FP16 on CUDA and FP32 on CPU.
  • Looks in the local HF cache first (local_files_only=True), then optionally downloads. Every failure is captured: no package, no cache, no network, bad weights → the heuristic engine is used and attributes_meta.clip.error explains why.
  • Concurrent requests never queue behind a download: while the model is loading, other requests use the heuristic immediately.
  • Prompt-conditioned on the predicted species (cattle / buffalo):
Field Labels Prompt gender Female "a side profile photo of a female dairy {species} cow with an udder, slender neck, and feminine face" gender Male "a side profile photo of a muscular male {species} bull or ox with a heavy neck, large hump, and broad head" age Calf (< 1 yr) "a photo of a small young baby calf with short legs, small head, and no horn development" age Young (1–3 yrs) "a photo of a medium-sized young heifer or sub-adult {species} with developing horns and lean body" age Adult (> 3 yrs) "a photo of a fully grown mature adult {species} with full body mass and developed horns"
  • Probabilities are softmax(logits_per_image / temperature); temperature is ATTRIBUTES_CLIP_TEMPERATURE (default 1.0).

docs.title: Engine B — morphological heuristic (fallback / Fast Mode)
docs.text:
Uses only signals already computed:

  • Trait activations — hump size, horn development, dewlap, body size.
  • Subject geometry — foreground bounding box from border-colour segmentation (subject_stats): a compact, tall silhouette nudges toward calf/young.
  • Breed prior — dairy breeds (DAIRY_BREEDS: Gir, Sahiwal, Murrah, Mehsana, …) start from an ≈85% adult-female prior, matching commercial dairy imagery.

Scores are additive log-odds → softmax, then shrunk toward uncertainty (confidence ceiling ≈ 88% gender / 82% age) because this is a prior, not a measurement. The payload is marked method: "morphological_heuristic" and requires_confirmation: true so the UI can ask the farmer to confirm with one tap.

  "gender": {
    "label": "Female (Cow)",

  },

    "label": "Adult (> 3 yrs)",
    "short_label": "Adult",
    "confidence": 89.1,
    "method": "clip_zeroshot",

  },

docs.title: 7. Limitations (read before quoting a farmer)
docs.text:
• Gender/age were not trained. They are CLIP guesses or transparent priors. Treat them as triage hints, not veterinary facts; the API says so via method / requires_confirmation.
  • Udder visibility is the main gender cue and is often hidden by the animal's stance; the heuristic uses hump/dewlap/size proxies instead.
  • Age is a visual stage estimate. Dentition (teeth) remains the only reliable field method.
  • Traits come from auxiliary heads trained on breed-level labels; they describe breed-typical morphology, not this individual's exact measurements.
  • Pad-to-square changes the input distribution relative to the exported ONNX preprocessor; keep BREEDID_PAD_TO_SQUARE=0 where bit-exact parity matters (e.g. ONNX parity tests).

docs.title: Breed Knowledge Base & Farmer Advisory
docs.text:
Every prediction is enriched with practical, offline guidance for farmers and the general public — no retraining, no extra model, no network call.

breed prediction ──► src/breed_knowledge.py ──► advisory (gender × age)
                     data/breed_knowledge.json

Coverage: all 68 classifier breeds (50 cattle + 18 buffalo) plus the crossbred/alias classes holstein_friesian and jersey.

docs.title: What each breed entry contains
docs.text:
Field Example display_name "Gir" local_names {"en": "Gir", "hi": "गीर", "ta": "கிர்"} origin_region "Saurashtra — Junagadh, Amreli, Bhavnagar and Porbandar, Gujarat" utility_type "Milch (Dairy)", "Draught (Work)", "Dual-Purpose", "Ornamental / Dwarf Dairy" milk_yield daily litres, lactation kg, fat %, lactation length, β-casein note (numeric ranges included for income maths) physical_markers 3 bullets for visual verification, derived from data/breed_traits.json feeding_and_care green/dry fodder, concentrate, mineral mixture, water (kg or g/day) climate_and_disease_resistance heat tolerance, tick/parasite resistance, disease notes, housing, smallholder suitability estimated_market_price_inr "₹45,000 - ₹100,000" (numeric range included) govt_schemes RGM, NLM, NADCP, KCC-AH, DIDF, ICAR conservation support data_confidence "curated" or "regional_default"

Data policy. Curated entries follow NBAGR/ICAR breed descriptions and standard Indian feeding norms (2–2.5 % body-weight dry matter, 0.4 kg concentrate per litre of milk above 5 L). Rare breeds without reliable published production data use the utility template and are explicitly flagged regional_default — the UI tells the farmer so. Prices, yields and vaccination timings vary by farm and district, and every advisory ends with a disclaimer.

docs.title: Advisory engine
docs.text:
get_farmer_advisory(species, breed_slug, gender, age_group) builds a context matrix. It is pure dictionary assembly (~0.1 ms), so the UI can re-render on a toggle without touching the image model.

Context Emphasis Female + Adult Lactation management, expected yield/fat, concentrate top-up (0.4 kg/L above 5 L), calcium + mineral mixture, mastitis prevention, drying-off, calving interval, milk income estimate Female + Young Heifer growth ration (400–600 g/day gain), target breeding weight, age at first calving by breed type, estrous/heat signs Male + Adult Milk is hidden (not the relevant metric); draught work capacity, safe load, yoke/hoof care, breeding-bull and semen value Male + Young Bull-calf vs draught-ox decision, castration timing, growth target, temperament handling Calf (any gender) Colostrum in the first 1–2 h, 10 % body-weight milk, calf starter, deworming on day 10/30/60, FMD/HS/BQ calendar, brucellosis for female calves Unspecified General breed briefing when the model's gender/age estimate is unavailable

Returned shape:

  "breed": {"species": "Cattle", "slug": "gir", "display_name": "Gir",

            "origin_region": "...", "utility_type": "Milch (Dairy)",
            "data_confidence": "curated"},
  "context": {"gender": "Female", "age_group": "Adult"},
  "headline": "Gir adult female — protect lactation ...",
  "priority_actions": ["...", "..."],
  "nutrition": {"green_fodder": "22 - 30 kg/day", "...": "..."},
  "health": {"vaccination": [], "watch_for": [], "housing": "..."},

docs.text:
POST /api/predict now includes a knowledge block computed from the predicted breed and the estimated/confirmed gender and age:

{
  "top_breed": "Gir",
  "gender": {"short_label": "Female", "...": "..."},
  "age_group": {"short_label": "Adult", "...": "..."},
  "knowledge": {"headline": "Gir adult female — protect lactation ...", "...": "..."}

docs.text:
data/breed_knowledge.json is created automatically on first use:

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Figures are typical ranges for the breed, not this animal's measurement.
  • Market prices are indicative 2024–25 farm-gate ranges and move with locality, lactation stage, fat % and festival demand.
  • Vaccination schedules must follow the local State Animal Husbandry Department; NADCP timing can differ by district.
  • regional_default breeds (e.g. Bhelai, Ghumsari, Marathwada) have thin published data and are flagged as estimates.

docs.text:

  • Added dynamic female-adult, male-adult, calf, young and fallback advisory cards; calf responses include a vaccination/deworming timeline. Milk yield is hidden for males and calves; draught advice is hidden for females and calves.
  • Added en/ta/hi copy, localized breed names and scheme names, CORS *, 5-second client timeout and offline fallback.
  • Added breed-classifier-react/src/services/onlineAdvisory.js with fetchAdvisoryData(...); it never throws and degrades to an on-device-only message when offline or slow.
  • Breed Tips now opens whenever the device is online; the legacy Online Mode / backend-health gate was removed for this free API, and offline copy was updated.
  • Deployed the API to Vercel production at https://advisory-api-bharaths31s-projects.vercel.app/api/advisory and wired that URL as the default advisory endpoint in the Android client. The Breed Tips modal now renders the live advisory cards, vaccination timeline and schemes.
  • Added a browser landing page at / so the deployment base URL is no longer a 404, and disabled Vercel Authentication protection for public API access.
  • Verified with 7 API tests, a live local HTTP request, and a browser import of the Android client.

docs.title: 2026-11-05 — Center-focused guardrail, top-k OOD and selfie blocker
docs.text:
• Center-focused Stage A: straight-edge and flat-patch checks now run on the central 180×180 region, with only a high-threshold global fallback. Barn roofs, fences, sky and other border clutter no longer reject a valid animal.
  • Human selfie gate: checkHumanSelfie() uses the browser FaceDetector when available, then a pure-JS YCbCr fallback (central skin ratio, 5×5 skin smoothness, bilateral skin symmetry, dark hair cap and eye/brow density). Close-up selfies return human_or_selfie before any breed prediction.
  • Top-k OOD: single-class Z_peak/Z_max rejection was replaced by top-3/top-5 breed-mass checks plus a relaxed entropy ceiling. docs.title: 2026-11-05 — Multi-stage object/monitor guardrail and biometric age/gender
docs.text:

Runs on the prepared 260×260 canvas before a prediction is accepted.
  • Stage B logit gate: normalized 68-class entropy, top-logit Z-score peak, binary-confidence floor, energy and MSP checks. Rejections return rejected: true with no species/breed and a localized reason.

Valid cattle pass; the screen screenshot, human selfie and goat test image are rejected.

  • Result UI: a rejection card replaces the dossier for rejected images with a localized reason and retry action; rejected scans are not added to recent scans. Gender/age remain read-only.

docs.title: 2026-11-04 — Self-describing .pt / .onnx models (zero external JSON)
docs.text:
• src/model_introspect.py: unified loading/introspection for PyTorch and ONNX. Architecture is auto-detected from tensor shapes (backbone from the first MBConv width, CBAM vs SE from the spatial conv, head widths/counts from the final layers) and from the ONNX graph (input resolution, output widths, float16 I/O). Returns a LoadedModelBundle with the correct transform, inverse class maps, embedded OOD thresholds and a Dev-Console spec summary.
  • Normalization fix: bundle.transform stops at ToTensor() when the graph already bakes ImageNet mean/std (_MobileOutputs, *_mobile* ONNX), eliminating double normalization. Caller-normalized .pt / _RawOutputs ONNX still get Normalize.
  • scripts/embed_metadata.py: --all, --file, --inspect CLI that writes class maps, preprocessing, resolution, normalization mode and OOD thresholds into existing files. .pt metadata lives in ckpt["model_meta"] (TorchScript uses an extra model_meta.json); ONNX uses metadata_props. Writes are atomic and weights are untouched.
  • Exports/training: src/export.py embeds metadata after ONNX, ONNX-INT8 and FP16 exports and into portable model.pt; src/train.py embeds it in every checkpoint and re-embeds calibrated OOD thresholds after training.
  • Runtime: test_model.py and server/ now load through LoadedModelBundle, use per-model class maps (50- and 42-class models can coexist), cast float16 ONNX inputs automatically, and prefer embedded OOD thresholds (legacy JSON is still honoured for old artifacts). Uploads are embedded + validated on arrival.
  • Robustness: legacy 7-layer binary heads (v17/v22/v9 portable bundles) are rebuilt from tensor keys; class maps are only accepted when their length matches the head width.
  • Docs: new Self-Describing Models page.

docs.title: 2026-09-24 — Breed trait heads, group-aware splits, hard negatives, tooling
docs.text:
• Breed trait auxiliary heads (D2, opt-in --trait-weight, suggested 0.1): new src/traits.py + scripts/make_trait_template.py generating data/breed_traits.json (75 breeds × hump/horn/coat/ear/dewlap/face/size, all empty for you to fill). Trait classifiers run on the pooled 1280-d features, masked loss ignores empty traits, and per-trait val accuracy is logged each eval. Training-only; excluded from export (verified).
  • Group-aware splits (E1, --dedup-splits): dHash (no external deps) groups near-duplicates (Hamming ≤ DEDUP_HAMMING=4) within each breed so twins never cross train/val/test; hashes cached in data/splits/hashes.csv; long-tail minimums preserved.
  • Val-noise warning (E3): prepare_splits prints min/median val images per breed and warns when any breed has < VAL_MIN_WARN (2).
  • SupCon hard negatives (D4): supervised_contrastive_loss up-weights confused-pair negatives (CONTRASTIVE_HARD_NEG_WEIGHT=2.0); --hard-pairs loads confusion_pairs.json produced by the new scripts/mine_confusions.py.
  • Per-group LR logging (F4): train_phase prints + logs each optimizer group's LR and parameter count at phase start.
  • Tooling (G2/G4): scripts/mine_confusions.py (top-30 confused breed pairs as global ids), scripts/run_ablations.sh / .ps1 (quarter-data sweep R0→R7, --dry-run supported), plus scripts/view_logs.py.
  • Cosine/ArcFace breed heads (D3, --cosine-head): CosineHead replaces the final Linear on cattle/buffalo heads. Forward is margin-free scaled cosine (scale=30), so inference/export are unchanged; the additive angular margin (COSINE_MARGIN=0.3) is ramped over the first COSINE_MARGIN_RAMP_EPOCHS=10 phase-2 epochs and applied to the target class inside the loss. export and test_model.py auto-detect cosine checkpoints (final head layer has no bias) and build the matching model.
  • Tests: scripts/test_master_cpu.py now 61 checks (traits, dedup, hard negatives, cosine head, logger, mixing, EMA, metrics, transforms, CBAM identity).

Stdout/stderr are tee'd into run.log (tqdm \r frames collapsed).

docs.title: 2026-09-24 — Blocking bug fixes, flip+RRC on by default, dataset inventory
docs.text:
• Missing src/run_utils.py crash fixed: the file is now present and local_train.py preflights every required src/ module, raising a clear "sync these files" error instead of ModuleNotFoundError.
  • SAMPLER_BETA import added to src/train.py (it was used in main() but never imported → would crash).
  • Mixing gate fixed: run_epoch gated mixing on desc.startswith("train"), which never matched phase{n} e{i}/{N}, so --mix was dead code. Replaced with an explicit training=True flag and a mix_stats counter; the eval log now prints mix=on (n/N batches) only when mixing actually ran.
  • find_latest_checkpoint pattern fixed to match timestamped names (lite2_phase2_best_V3.pt), and resolve_checkpoint(path_or_tag) added so --run-tag V3 works with --checkpoint in export/evaluate/parity_check.
  • Class-count fail-fast: prepare_* now raises with explicit extra/missing breed names and prints names shared across species (bargur).
  • Flip + mild RRC ON by default (AUG_HORIZONTAL_FLIP, AUG_RANDOM_RESIZED_CROP) — they don't mix content between breeds. Colour jitter / RandAugment / mix stay off. --no-augment forces all off.
  • RRC ratio tightened to (0.92, 1.08) and hue capped at 0.02 (--allow-hue to raise) so body proportions and coat colour survive.
  • Breed-aware augmentation: BREED_AUG_POLICY / COAT_COLOUR_BREEDS (coat-colour breeds skip colour jitter), applied per sample in the Dataset.
  • Pad-to-square (--pad-to-square): resize long side + pad to square, keeping full-body side profiles.
  • CBAM/SE identity at init (CBAM_IDENTITY_INIT): zero-init final layers with x*(1+gate), so attention no longer distorts pretrained features during phase-1 warmup.
  • Metrics: combined_top3/5 are now species-aware over the soft-routed 75-way scores; the old true-species versions are combined_top3_oracle / combined_top5_oracle. Added val_min_per_breed / val_median_per_breed and fixed the pred_hist_entropy comment.
  • Dataset inventory: build_dataset_inventory() in local_train.py and the Colab downloader writes data/dataset_inventory/<dataset>.json with breed, species (cattle/buffalo), count, and per-image resolution for both datasets and the merged tree.
  • Tests: scripts/test_master_cpu.py (40 CPU-only synthetic checks).

docs.title: 2026-09-23 — Tail-bias regression fix: single imbalance mechanism, safe mixing, EMA, soft routing, timestamped outputs
docs.text:
Diagnosed from a 10-photo ONNX batch test (0/10 correct; top-5 dominated by rare breeds; a Gir bull predicted as a rare breed) that regressed after the 2026-09-21 overhaul.

Imbalance (src/config.py, src/data_pipeline.py, src/train.py): - LOGIT_ADJUST is now False by default — the effective-number sampler is the single long-tail mechanism. Enabling both double-corrects and over-predicts rare breeds at inference. --logit-adjust re-enables it; its prior is computed from the effective sampled distribution (--logit-adjust-prior sampled|raw), never raw counts. Startup prints the active mechanism and prior max/min ratio. - Fixed _effective_num_weights divide-by-zero for classes absent from train (previously produced NaN logit-adjustment priors).

Mixing (src/config.py, src/data_pipeline.py, src/train.py): - CutMix/MixUp now pair within the same species (_pairing_perm), so binary labels stay one-hot and breed targets stay proper distributions. - Strength reduced: CUTMIX_MIXUP_PROB 0.5→0.25, CUTMIX_ALPHA 1.0→0.4, MIXUP_ALPHA 0.3→0.2. Rare-class guard kept. - MIX_OFF_LAST_FRAC=0.15 disables mixing for the last 15% of phase 2.

Augmentation OFF by default (src/config.py, src/data_pipeline.py): - flip / ColorJitter / RandAugment / RandomResizedCrop / mixing are opt-in via --mix --flip --color-jitter --randaugment --rrc --augment-all. With all off, the train transform equals the eval transform.

EMA (src/train.py): - Updated once per optimizer step (was twice per micro-batch with grad_accum=2), with warm-up decay_t = min(0.999,(1+t)/(10+t)). - Startup prints steps/epoch, total optimizer steps and the EMA time constant, warning if it exceeds 25% of phase-2 steps. Every eval logs BOTH raw and EMA metrics and saves whichever scores better.

Checkpoint selection (src/config.py, src/metrics.py): - BEST_METRIC="blended_score" = 0.5·macro-F1 + 0.5·soft-routed top-1. - Each eval also logs few/medium/many-shot accuracy and predicted-histogram entropy.

Preprocessing (test_model.py, src/config.py): - test_model.py now uses the eval transform (shortest-side resize + CenterCrop) instead of a square Resize((260,260)). New EVAL_MATCH_TRAIN_RESOLUTION to test Resize(288)+CenterCrop(260) at eval.

Timestamped outputs (src/run_utils.py, new): - Checkpoints/exports/metrics carry a run id (DD-MM-YYYY-HH-MM or --run-tag) and never overwrite previous runs. src.export / src.evaluate / src.parity_check / local_train.py auto-discover the newest checkpoint.

Tooling (run-later): scripts/audit_data.py, scripts/diagnose_model.py, scripts/onnx_parity_10.py, scripts/test_fixes_cpu.py.

docs.title: 2026-09-21 — Long-Tail Accuracy Overhaul: Logit Adjustment, Feature Metric Learning, Soft Routing, 70/15/15 Splits
docs.text:
Motivated by a graph-assisted gap analysis: phase-2 best val top-1 was 0.578 (binary 0.95, cattle 0.59, buffalo 0.61), with 21+ indigenous cattle breeds carrying ≤14 images against gir=768, and the old 85/10/5 split leaving many rare breeds with zero test images.

Config (src/config.py): - SAMPLER_BETA 0.999 → 0.99 (softer effective-number oversampling). - Split ratios 70/15/15 (was 85/10/5); PHASE2_EPOCHS 60 → 80. - New: LOGIT_ADJUST/LOGIT_ADJUST_TAU, CONTRASTIVE_WEIGHT/CONTRASTIVE_TEMPERATURE, RARE_CLASS_THRESHOLD, PROJECTION_DIM, BEST_METRIC="balanced_score", and saturated-binary loss weights (*_FINAL, BINARY_SATURATION_ACC).

Imbalance (src/data_pipeline.py, src/train.py): - Logit adjustment (Menon et al., ICLR 2021): tau·log(prior) added to breed logits during training only, from smoothed train priors (compute_class_priors). - Long-tail split minimums: every (species, breed) with ≥3 images now gets ≥1 val and ≥1 test image; fixed grouping to key on (species, breed) because bargur exists under both species. - Rare-class mixing guard: breeds below RARE_CLASS_THRESHOLD (30 train images) are excluded from CutMix/MixUp (compute_rare_classes + keep mask). - Adaptive loss weights: once binary_acc ≥ 0.95, weights switch from 0.15/0.50/0.35 to 0.05/0.55/0.40 to reallocate budget to the breed heads. - --no-mix now actually disables mixing (previously it only swapped the collate fn).

Feature learning (src/model.py, src/train.py): - New auxiliary projection head + supervised contrastive (SupCon) loss on the previously-unused pooled features (CONTRASTIVE_WEIGHT=0.2); skipped on mixed batches where labels are soft. Adds a dedicated optimizer param group.

Metrics & selection (src/metrics.py): - evaluate_epoch now reports per-head macro-F1, balanced accuracy, and soft-routed combined top-1 (p(species)·softmax(head)). - Checkpoints are selected on balanced_score = ½(cattle_macro_f1 + buffalo_macro_f1) instead of combined top-1, which was dominated by ~10 large breeds.

Soft routing: BreedClassifier.predict(), test_model.py, and both Flutter engines (android_tflite_engine.dart, web_tfjs_engine.dart) now mix p(species)·softmax(head) across all 75 breeds instead of hard binary argmax, removing two-stage routing error propagation.

Export (src/export.py, local_train.py): - _sanitize_state_dict strips _orig_mod./module. prefixes and QAT fake_quant/activation_post_process/fused-BN keys, so phase-3/QAT and compiled checkpoints no longer crash ONNX/FP16/INT8 export. - local_train.py prefers the phase-2 (EMA) checkpoint and exports INT8 via the converter-side PTQ path (--mode onnx-int8), not the removed --mode int8.

docs.title: 2026-09-20 — Accuracy/Efficiency Overhaul: Distillation, EMA Fix, Mobile INT8 Exports
docs.text:
Training (src/train.py): - Fixed a critical EMA bug: the EMA now updates BatchNorm buffers (running mean/var) in addition to parameters; num_batches_tracked is hard-copied. Previously every phase-2 checkpoint exported stale BN stats, silently degrading validation accuracy and the deployed model. - Knowledge distillation: new --teacher, --teacher-backbone, --teacher-attention flags. Loss = (1-α)·masked_hard_CE + α·T²·masked_KL(teacher‖student) on all three heads (α=0.7, T=4.0). Train a lite4 teacher, distill into the unchanged lite2 student — teacher accuracy at zero on-device cost. - QAT is now opt-in (--include-qat); default training is a clean 2-phase run. QAT uses per-tensor observers (fixes the Unsupported qscheme: per_channel_affine conversion failure) and starts from the best phase-2 EMA checkpoint instead of final-epoch weights. - Binary-head species balancing: per-batch re-weighting (BALANCE_BINARY_HEAD=True) neutralizes the 57:18 breed-count species prior.

Data (src/data_pipeline.py): - Sampler switched to effective-number-of-samples weighting (SAMPLER_BETA=0.999) — softens over-oversampling of 5-image breeds. - CutMix/MixUp probability raised 0.25 → 0.5 (CUTMIX_MIXUP_PROB). - All prepare_*_splits() create the split directory if missing.

Export (src/export.py): - New --mode tflite: ONNX → onnx2tf → TFLite FP32 + full-integer INT8 PTQ (float32 [0,1] I/O), emits labels_*.txt, auto-copies into flutter_app/assets/models/. - New --mode onnx-int8: QDQ static quantization for ONNX Runtime Mobile (per-channel weights, calibrated on real train images). - ImageNet normalization is baked into mobile graphs — the Flutter app's pixel/255 preprocessing is now exactly correct with zero app changes. - Removed the broken x86 PTQ --mode int8 path (guidance stub remains).

Verification (src/parity_check.py, new): - python -m src.parity_check compares fp32 PyTorch vs TFLite/ONNX INT8 on val/test (training-equivalent metrics) or --synthetic N for artifact-only parity. Gate: INT8 within 1 pt combined_top1 of fp32.

Measured: ONNX INT8 = 7.10 MB (from 25.65 MB FP32); fp32 ONNX exact parity; INT8 max |Δlogit| ≈ 0.05–0.07 on random inputs; end-to-end smoke training (2-phase, distillation, QAT→INT8) verified on CPU.

docs.title: 2026-09-15 — Architecture Improvements, EMA, & ImageNet Normalization Fix
docs.text:
Architecture: - Deepened cattle_head and buffalo_head with an extra hidden layer (BREED_DIM // 2). - Integrated BatchNorm1d into both breed classification heads for better convergence and to prevent covariate shift. - Adjusted dropout values for the new layers (0.3 for first, 0.2 for second).

Training Pipeline: - Phase 1 (Warmup): Now trains all three heads (binary, cattle, buffalo) to build robust initial representations, instead of just the binary head. - Differential Learning Rates (Phase 2): Applied fine-grained LR scaling (backbone: 0.1x, attention: 0.5x, heads: 1.0x). - EMA: Integrated Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with a decay of 0.999 for model weights during Phase 2 to drastically improve evaluation stability and generalization. - Bug Fix: Fixed critical bug where the training pipeline lacked transforms.Normalize() using ImageNet statistics, aligning it properly with inference logic. - Reconfigured default portable export to securely capture the best weights from Phase 2 instead of Phase 3, avoiding the massive accuracy drop previously caused by aggressive INT8 QAT, while maintaining a very lightweight model footprint (~27.3 MB) ready for Android deployment.

Metrics: - Added vectorized Top-5 combined accuracy tracking to evaluate_epoch() alongside Top-1 and Top-3.

docs.title: 1. Automated Pipeline (Recommended)
docs.text:
The fastest path from zero to a trained model. Handles everything automatically.

python local_train.py --quarter-data

docs.title: 3.5 Training
docs.text:
# Smoke test — 5 images/breed, 1 epoch per phase
python -m src.train --smoke-test

# Quarter-data training
python -m src.train --quarter-data

# Half-data training
python -m src.train --half-data

# Full training (2 phases: warmup + multi-task fine-tune with EMA)
python -m src.train --backbone lite2

# Teacher run (bigger backbone, used for distillation)

  --teacher outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt

docs.title: Known Constraints & Gotchas
docs.text:
1. QAT + CUDA AMP conflict Phase 3 (QAT, opt-in via --include-qat) disables the AMP (GradScaler) because quantization observers are not compatible with mixed precision. This is intentional and handled automatically — AMP is active for Phases 1–2, disabled for Phase 3.

1b. EMA must include BatchNorm buffers, once per optimizer step (src/train.py) The phase-2 EMA updates parameters and BN running stats (num_batches_tracked is hard-copied), once per optimizer step (not per micro-batch), with warm-up decay_t = min(0.999, (1+t)/(10+t)). Removing the buffer sync corrupts every phase-2 checkpoint with stale BN statistics while validation still looks plausible — keep the sync and the per-step placement.

1c. Mobile artifacts are static batch-1 with [0,1] input TFLite/ONNX-INT8 exports bake ImageNet normalization into the graph and expect RGB float32 in [0,1] (the Flutter app's pixel/255). Keep output names/order stable (binary, cattle, buffalo) when editing _MobileOutputs in src/export.py.

1d. QAT/compiled checkpoints are re-exportable via the sanitizer src/export._sanitize_state_dict strips _orig_mod./module. prefixes and QAT observer/fused keys, then loads with strict=False (training-only projection_head.* tolerated); it raises only on genuinely missing non-projection keys. Export the phase-2 EMA checkpoint for best accuracy.

1e. TFLite toolchain is optional and Python-version sensitive --mode tflite needs tensorflow + onnx2tf (see requirements.txt). --mode onnx-int8 needs only onnxruntime. TensorFlow is not installable on Python 3.14 — run TFLite conversion from a Python ≤3.13 venv (the Windows venv is 3.13) or Colab.

1f. Preprocessing must match eval Eval uses shortest-side Resize(260) + CenterCrop(260) + ImageNet normalize; test_model.py and the Flutter preprocessor match. Square Resize((260,260)) distorts aspect ratio and wrecked external-batch predictions before the 2026-09-23 fix.

1g. Outputs are timestamped per run Checkpoints/exports/metrics carry a run id (DD-MM-YYYY-HH-MM, config RUN_ID_FORMAT). Colons are illegal in Windows filenames, hence -. src/run_utils provides make_run_id/timestamped/unique_path/find_latest_checkpoint; tools auto-discover the newest checkpoint.

  1. Backbone weights are included in the repository efficientnet_lite2.pth and efficientnet_lite4.pth are tracked in git. No separate download is required. Without them, the backbone would train from scratch (significantly worse accuracy). local_train.py verifies their presence at startup.

  2. torch.compile crashes on Windows Windows lacks native Triton support, causing BackendCompilerFailed: Cannot find a working triton installation when torch.compile is used. src/train.py automatically detects os.name == 'nt' and falls back to eager execution. Use --no-compile to force this behavior manually on any platform.

  3. torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead") OOM on T4 (Colab) reduce-overhead mode uses CUDA Graphs, which pre-allocates significant VRAM during the backwards pass. On 15 GB T4 GPUs, this causes OutOfMemoryError during Phase 2. The default torch.compile(model) (no mode argument) does not use CUDA Graphs and avoids the OOM.

  4. Fixed head sizes regardless of data mode Model heads are always sized for 57 cattle + 18 buffalo = 75 classes, even during smoke test or subset training. Unused class outputs simply receive no gradient from those images. This is by design — the model architecture is identical across all data modes.

  5. WeightedRandomSampler is the single long-tail mechanism (default on) Training oversamples rare breeds using effective-number-of-samples weighting (SAMPLER_BETA=0.99). Logit adjustment is OFF by default (LOGIT_ADJUST=False) because the sampler already rebalances every batch — enabling both double-corrects and over-predicts rare breeds at inference. If enabled with --logit-adjust, its prior comes from the effective sampled distribution, and absent classes get the smallest present prior (never NaN). Breeds below RARE_CLASS_THRESHOLD train images are excluded from CutMix/MixUp. Evaluation uses no sampling — the test set reflects the natural distribution. The binary head is additionally species-balanced per batch (BALANCE_BINARY_HEAD=True).

  6. Soft cross-entropy (not hard labels) Training supports soft label vectors because CutMix/MixUp produce fractional labels (e.g., 60% breed A / 40% breed B). Hard one-hot labels are a special case and work identically with soft_ce. Mixing is off by default and, when enabled, pairs within a species so labels stay well-formed.

  7. Portable export requires BreedClassifier class The portable bundle saves state_dict (not TorchScript). Loading requires importing BreedClassifier from src/model.py. For completely framework-free inference, use the ONNX export instead.

  8. Smoke test uses ALL 75 breed classes Even with only 5 images per breed, the class maps include all breeds from the full dataset. Architecture is identical to full training. This ensures smoke test results are a valid proxy for the real training configuration.

  9. Dataset zip cleanup local_train.py deletes the downloaded breed-cattle-buffalo.zip after extraction to save disk space. If extraction fails partway, delete the zip and the incomplete data/raw/ directory, then re-run.

  10. data/splits/ is regenerated on every training run The CSV splits are regenerated from scratch at the start of each src.train run. This ensures the correct stratified split for the selected data mode. Do not manually edit files in data/splits/.

  11. Windows: curl syntax differs On Windows PowerShell, the built-in curl is an alias for Invoke-WebRequest. Use curl.exe explicitly, or use Invoke-WebRequest syntax. local_train.py uses the requests Python library internally to avoid this issue.

class CosineHead(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, scale=COSINE_SCALE):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.empty(out_features, in_features))
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.weight)
        self.scale = float(scale)

    def forward(self, x):
        cos = F.linear(F.normalize(x, dim=1), F.normalize(self.weight, dim=1))
        return self.scale * cos

def _make_breed_head(feature_dim, num_classes, dropout, cosine=False,
                     scale=COSINE_SCALE, breed_dim=BREED_DIM):
    layers = [
        nn.Linear(feature_dim, breed_dim),
        nn.BatchNorm1d(breed_dim),
        nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
        nn.Dropout(dropout),
        nn.Linear(breed_dim, breed_dim // 2),
        nn.BatchNorm1d(breed_dim // 2),
        nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
        nn.Dropout(0.2),
    ]
    layers.append(CosineHead(breed_dim // 2, num_classes, scale) if cosine
                  else nn.Linear(breed_dim // 2, num_classes))
    return nn.Sequential(*layers)

class BreedClassifier(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, backbone="lite2", num_cattle=NUM_CATTLE_BREEDS,
                 num_buffalo=NUM_BUFFALO_BREEDS, cbam_stage=CBAM_AFTER_STAGE,
                 attention="cbam", activation="relu6", pretrained_path=None,
                 dropout=DROPOUT, cosine_head=False, cosine_scale=COSINE_SCALE,
                 binary_dim=BINARY_DIM, breed_dim=BREED_DIM):
        super().__init__()
        self.cosine_head = bool(cosine_head)
        self.cosine_scale = float(cosine_scale)
        self.backbone = EfficientNetLite(arch=backbone, activation=activation)
        self.cbam_stage = cbam_stage
        stage_channels = self.backbone.stage_channels[cbam_stage]
        self.attention = build_attention(attention, stage_channels)
        feature_dim = self.backbone.head_channels

        self.avg_pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.binary_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, binary_dim),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(binary_dim),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Dropout(p=dropout),
            nn.Linear(binary_dim, binary_dim // 2),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(binary_dim // 2),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Dropout(p=0.2),
            nn.Linear(binary_dim // 2, 2),
        )
        self.cattle_head = _make_breed_head(feature_dim, num_cattle, dropout,
                                            self.cosine_head, self.cosine_scale,
                                            breed_dim=breed_dim)
        self.buffalo_head = _make_breed_head(feature_dim, num_buffalo, dropout,
                                             self.cosine_head, self.cosine_scale,
                                             breed_dim=breed_dim)

        self.projection_head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, feature_dim),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Linear(feature_dim, PROJECTION_DIM),
        )

        if pretrained_path:
            n = load_backbone_weights(self.backbone, pretrained_path)
            print(f"[model] loaded {n} tensors from {pretrained_path}")

    def forward_features(self, x):
        feats = self.backbone.forward_until(x, self.cbam_stage)
        feats = self.attention(feats)
        feats = self.backbone.forward_from(feats, self.cbam_stage + 1)
        return self.avg_pool(feats).flatten(1)

    def forward(self, x):
        pooled = self.forward_features(x)
        return {
            "binary": self.binary_head(pooled),
            "cattle": self.cattle_head(pooled),
            "buffalo": self.buffalo_head(pooled),
            "features": pooled,
            "embedding": self.projection_head(pooled),
        }

    @torch.no_grad()
    def predict(self, x):
        out = self.forward(x)
        p_species = F.softmax(out["binary"], dim=1)
        p_cattle = F.softmax(out["cattle"], dim=1)
        p_buffalo = F.softmax(out["buffalo"], dim=1)
        return torch.cat([p_species[:, 0:1] * p_cattle,
                          p_species[:, 1:2] * p_buffalo], dim=1)

    @torch.no_grad()
    def predict_safe(self, x, ood_detector=None):
        out = self.forward(x)

        if ood_detector is not None:
            is_ood, score, details = ood_detector.is_ood(
                out["binary"], out["cattle"], out["buffalo"]
            )
            if is_ood:

                n_total = out["cattle"].shape[1] + out["buffalo"].shape[1]
                return torch.zeros(x.shape[0], n_total, device=x.device), {
                    "ood": True, "ood_score": score, **details
                }

        p_species = F.softmax(out["binary"], dim=1)
        p_cattle = F.softmax(out["cattle"], dim=1)
        p_buffalo = F.softmax(out["buffalo"], dim=1)
        combined = torch.cat([p_species[:, 0:1] * p_cattle,
                              p_species[:, 1:2] * p_buffalo], dim=1)
        return combined, {"ood": False}

    @torch.no_grad()
    def predict_guarded(self, x, pil_img=None, image_bytes=None,
                        ood_detector=None, guardrail=None):
        out = self.forward(x)
        if guardrail is None:
            from .input_guardrails import get_guardrail_engine
            guardrail = get_guardrail_engine()
        verdict = guardrail.validate_image(
            image_bytes, pil_img, model_outputs=out, ood_detector=ood_detector)
        return out, verdict

    def freeze_backbone(self):
        for p in self.backbone.parameters():
            p.requires_grad = False
        for p in self.attention.parameters():
            p.requires_grad = False

    def freeze_all(self):
        for p in self.parameters():
            p.requires_grad = False

    def unfreeze_all(self):
        for p in self.parameters():
            p.requires_grad = True

    def backbone_eval(self):
        self.backbone.eval()
        self.attention.eval()

    def backbone_train(self):
        self.backbone.train()
        self.attention.train()

class ChannelAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels, reduction=16, identity_init=CBAM_IDENTITY_INIT):
        super().__init__()
        mid = max(1, channels // reduction)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(channels, mid, 1, bias=False),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(mid, channels, 1, bias=False),
        )
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()
        self.identity_init = identity_init
        if identity_init:
            _zero_init_last(self.mlp)

    def forward(self, x):
        avg = torch.mean(x, dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)
        mx = torch.amax(x, dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)
        att = self.mlp(avg) + self.mlp(mx)
        if self.identity_init:

            gate = 2.0 * self.sigmoid(att) - 1.0
            return x * (1.0 + gate)
        return x * self.sigmoid(att)

class SpatialAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, kernel_size=7, identity_init=CBAM_IDENTITY_INIT):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(2, 1, kernel_size, padding=kernel_size // 2, bias=False)
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()
        self.identity_init = identity_init
        if identity_init:
            nn.init.zeros_(self.conv.weight)

    def forward(self, x):
        avg = torch.mean(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
        mx = torch.amax(x, dim=1, keepdim=True)
        fused = torch.cat([avg, mx], dim=1)
        att = self.conv(fused)
        if self.identity_init:
            gate = 2.0 * self.sigmoid(att) - 1.0
            return x * (1.0 + gate)
        return x * self.sigmoid(att)

class CBAM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels, reduction=16, kernel_size=7,
                 identity_init=CBAM_IDENTITY_INIT):
        super().__init__()
        self.channel_attention = ChannelAttention(channels, reduction,
                                                  identity_init=identity_init)
        self.spatial_attention = SpatialAttention(kernel_size,
                                                  identity_init=identity_init)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.channel_attention(x)
        x = self.spatial_attention(x)
        return x

class PadToSquare:

    def __init__(self, size=IMAGE_SIZE, fill=None):
        self.size = int(size)
        self.fill = fill or tuple(int(round(m * 255)) for m in IMAGENET_MEAN)

    def __call__(self, img):
        w, h = img.size
        scale = self.size / max(w, h)
        nw, nh = max(1, round(w * scale)), max(1, round(h * scale))
        resized = img.resize((nw, nh), Image.BILINEAR)
        canvas = Image.new("RGB", (self.size, self.size), self.fill)
        canvas.paste(resized, ((self.size - nw) // 2, (self.size - nh) // 2))
        return canvas

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"PadToSquare({self.size}, fill={self.fill})"

def soft_ce(pred, target, label_smoothing=0.0, logit_prior=None, tau=0.0):
    if logit_prior is not None and tau:
        pred = pred + tau * logit_prior.to(pred.device).unsqueeze(0)
    if label_smoothing > 0.0:
        n_classes = pred.size(1)
        target = (1.0 - label_smoothing) * target + label_smoothing / n_classes
    return -(target * F.log_softmax(pred, dim=1)).sum(dim=1)

def masked_loss(out, labels, w_binary, w_cattle, w_buffalo,
                label_smoothing=0.0, logit_priors=None, adjust_tau=0.0,
                contrastive_weight=0.0, contrastive_temp=CONTRASTIVE_TEMPERATURE,
                mixed=False):
    cattle_prior = buffalo_prior = None
    if logit_priors is not None:
        cattle_prior = logit_priors.get("cattle")
        buffalo_prior = logit_priors.get("buffalo")

    ce_binary = soft_ce(out["binary"], labels["binary"], label_smoothing)
    if BALANCE_BINARY_HEAD:
        p_buffalo = labels["binary"][:, 1].clamp(0.0, 1.0)
        mean_buf = p_buffalo.mean().clamp(min=1e-4)
        mean_cat = (1.0 - p_buffalo).mean().clamp(min=1e-4)

        w_cat = 0.5 / mean_cat
        w_buf = 0.5 / mean_buf
        sample_w = w_cat * (1.0 - p_buffalo) + w_buf * p_buffalo
        ce_binary = (ce_binary * sample_w).sum() / sample_w.sum()
    else:
        ce_binary = ce_binary.mean()
    cattle_logits = out["cattle"]
    buffalo_logits = out["buffalo"]
    if _COSINE_SCALE is not None and _COSINE_MARGIN > 0:
        cattle_logits = _apply_cosine_margin(cattle_logits, labels["cattle"],
                                             _COSINE_MARGIN, _COSINE_SCALE)
        buffalo_logits = _apply_cosine_margin(buffalo_logits, labels["buffalo"],
                                              _COSINE_MARGIN, _COSINE_SCALE)
    ce_cattle = (soft_ce(cattle_logits, labels["cattle"], label_smoothing,
                         cattle_prior, adjust_tau) * labels["cattle_mask"])
    ce_buffalo = (soft_ce(buffalo_logits, labels["buffalo"], label_smoothing,
                          buffalo_prior, adjust_tau) * labels["buffalo_mask"])
    denom_c = labels["cattle_mask"].sum().clamp(min=1.0)
    denom_b = labels["buffalo_mask"].sum().clamp(min=1.0)
    ce_cattle = ce_cattle.sum() / denom_c
    ce_buffalo = ce_buffalo.sum() / denom_b
    total = (w_binary * ce_binary + w_cattle * ce_cattle + w_buffalo * ce_buffalo)
    total = total + _contrastive_term(out, labels, contrastive_weight,
                                      contrastive_temp, mixed)
    return total, ce_binary, ce_cattle, ce_buffalo

@torch.no_grad()
def full_evaluation(model, loader, device, num_cattle=NUM_CATTLE_BREEDS,
                    num_buffalo=NUM_BUFFALO_BREEDS):
    model.eval()
    cattle_cm = torch.zeros(num_cattle, num_cattle, dtype=torch.long)
    buffalo_cm = torch.zeros(num_buffalo, num_buffalo, dtype=torch.long)
    cattle_total = torch.zeros(num_cattle, dtype=torch.long)
    buffalo_total = torch.zeros(num_buffalo, dtype=torch.long)
    for images, labels in tqdm(loader, desc="eval detail", leave=False):
        images = images.to(device, non_blocking=True)
        is_cuda = (getattr(device, "type", str(device)) == "cuda" or str(device).startswith("cuda"))
        with torch.amp.autocast(device_type="cuda", enabled=is_cuda):
            out = model(images)
        bin_true = labels["binary"].argmax(1)
        cattle_true = labels["cattle"].argmax(1)
        buffalo_true = labels["buffalo"].argmax(1)
        cmask = labels["cattle_mask"] > 0.5
        bmask = labels["buffalo_mask"] > 0.5
        if cmask.any():
            pred = out["cattle"][cmask].argmax(1)
            true = cattle_true[cmask]
            for t, p in zip(true.tolist(), pred.tolist()):
                cattle_cm[t, p] += 1
                cattle_total[t] += 1
        if bmask.any():
            pred = out["buffalo"][bmask].argmax(1)
            true = buffalo_true[bmask]
            for t, p in zip(true.tolist(), pred.tolist()):
                buffalo_cm[t, p] += 1
                buffalo_total[t] += 1

    def per_class(cm, total):
        n_classes = cm.size(0)
        precision = []
        recall = []
        for c in range(n_classes):
            tp = cm[c, c].item()
            col = cm[:, c].sum().item()
            row = cm[c, :].sum().item()
            precision.append(tp / col if col else 0.0)
            recall.append(tp / row if row else 0.0)
        return {
            "precision": precision,
            "recall": recall,
            "counts": total.tolist(),
        }

    return {
        "cattle_cm": cattle_cm.numpy(),
        "buffalo_cm": buffalo_cm.numpy(),
        "cattle_total": cattle_total.numpy(),
        "buffalo_total": buffalo_total.numpy(),
        "cattle_per_class": per_class(cattle_cm, cattle_total),
        "buffalo_per_class": per_class(buffalo_cm, buffalo_total),
    }

class OODDetector:
    def __init__(self, temperature=1.0, energy_threshold=0.0, msp_threshold=0.0, binary_confidence_floor=0.0):
        self.T = float(temperature)
        self.energy_threshold = float(energy_threshold)
        self.msp_threshold = float(msp_threshold)
        self.binary_confidence_floor = float(binary_confidence_floor)

    def compute_energy(self, *logits_list):
        is_numpy = not isinstance(logits_list[0], torch.Tensor)
        if is_numpy:
            import numpy as np
            combined_logits = np.concatenate(logits_list, axis=-1)
            max_val = np.max(combined_logits / self.T, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
            sum_exp = np.sum(np.exp(combined_logits / self.T - max_val), axis=-1)
            energy = -self.T * (np.squeeze(max_val, axis=-1) + np.log(sum_exp))
            return energy
        else:
            combined_logits = torch.cat(logits_list, dim=-1)
            energy = -self.T * torch.logsumexp(combined_logits / self.T, dim=-1)
            return energy

    def compute_msp(self, binary_logits):
        is_numpy = not isinstance(binary_logits, torch.Tensor)
        if is_numpy:
            import numpy as np
            exp_logits = np.exp(binary_logits - np.max(binary_logits, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
            probs = exp_logits / np.sum(exp_logits, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
            return np.max(probs, axis=-1)
        else:
            probs = F.softmax(binary_logits, dim=-1)
            return torch.max(probs, dim=-1)[0]

    def is_ood(self, binary_logits, cattle_logits, buffalo_logits):
        energy = self.compute_energy(binary_logits, cattle_logits, buffalo_logits)
        msp = self.compute_msp(binary_logits)

        is_numpy = not isinstance(energy, torch.Tensor)
        if is_numpy:
            import numpy as np
            energy_val = float(np.atleast_1d(energy)[0])
            msp_val = float(np.atleast_1d(msp)[0])
        else:
            energy_val = energy.item() if energy.numel() == 1 else energy[0].item()
            msp_val = msp.item() if msp.numel() == 1 else msp[0].item()

        ood_by_energy = energy_val > self.energy_threshold
        ood_by_msp = msp_val < self.msp_threshold
        ood_by_binary_floor = msp_val < self.binary_confidence_floor
        is_ood_flag = ood_by_energy or ood_by_msp or ood_by_binary_floor

        return is_ood_flag, energy_val, {
            "energy": energy_val,

class InputGuardrailEngine:
    def validate_image(self, image_bytes: Optional[bytes], pil_img: Optional[Image.Image],
                       model_outputs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
                       ood_detector: Any = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        if not self.enabled:
            return self._accepted({}, started, skipped=True)

        image = pil_img
        if image is None and image_bytes:
            try:
                import io as _io
                image = Image.open(_io.BytesIO(image_bytes)).convert("RGB")
            except Exception:
                image = None

        stages: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        if image is not None:
            visual = self.validate_visual(image)
            stages["stage1_2"] = visual
            if visual["rejected"]:
                return self._rejected(visual, started, stages)
        else:
            stages["stage1_2"] = {"rejected": False, "details": {"skipped": "no image"}}

        if model_outputs is not None:
            model_verdict = self.validate_model_outputs(model_outputs, ood_detector)
            stages["stage3_4"] = model_verdict
            if model_verdict["rejected"]:
                return self._rejected(model_verdict, started, stages)
            details = model_verdict.get("details", {})
        else:
            details = {}

        return self._accepted(details, started, stages=stages)

    def validate_visual(self, pil_img: Image.Image) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not self.enabled:
            return {"rejected": False, "details": {"skipped": "disabled"}}

        started = time.perf_counter()
        if GUARDRAIL_PHOTOREALISM_ENABLED:
            realism = self._check_photorealism(pil_img)
            if realism["rejected"]:
                realism["stage"] = STAGE_NAMES[1]
                realism["latency_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
                return self._rejected(realism, started, {})

        human = self._check_human_or_selfie(pil_img)
        if human["rejected"]:
            human["stage"] = STAGE_NAMES[2]
            human["latency_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
            return self._rejected(human, started, {})
        return self._accepted(human.get("details", {}), started)

    def validate_model_outputs(self, model_outputs: Dict[str, Any],
                               ood_detector: Any = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        if not self.enabled:
            return {"rejected": False, "details": {"skipped": "disabled"}}
        started = time.perf_counter()
        feature = self._check_feature_and_entropy(model_outputs)
        if feature["rejected"]:
            feature["stage"] = STAGE_NAMES[3]
            feature["latency_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
            return self._rejected(feature, started, {})

        if ood_detector is not None:
            logit = self._check_logit_ood(model_outputs, ood_detector)
            if logit["rejected"]:
                logit["stage"] = STAGE_NAMES[4]
                logit["latency_ms"] = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
                return self._rejected(logit, started, {})

        return self._accepted(feature.get("details", {}), started)

export function preprocessToTensor(canvasOrImage, normalizationBaked = false) {
  const size = IMAGE_SIZE;
  const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
  canvas.width = size;
  canvas.height = size;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d", { willReadFrequently: true });
  ctx.drawImage(canvasOrImage, 0, 0, size, size);
  const { data } = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, size, size);
  const tensor = new Float32Array(3 * size * size);
  const plane = size * size;
  for (let i = 0, p = 0; i < plane; i += 1, p += 4) {
    const r = data[p] / 255;
    const g = data[p + 1] / 255;
    const b = data[p + 2] / 255;
    if (normalizationBaked) {
      tensor[i] = r;
      tensor[plane + i] = g;
      tensor[2 * plane + i] = b;
    } else {
      tensor[i] = (r - IMAGENET_MEAN[0]) / IMAGENET_STD[0];
      tensor[plane + i] = (g - IMAGENET_MEAN[1]) / IMAGENET_STD[1];
      tensor[2 * plane + i] = (b - IMAGENET_MEAN[2]) / IMAGENET_STD[2];
    }
  }
  return tensor;
}

export function estimateGenderAge({ breedSlug, canvas, imageMeta = {} }) {
  const stats = canvasStats(canvas);
  const aspect = Number(imageMeta.originalAspect || 1);
  const dairy = DAIRY_BREEDS.has(String(breedSlug || "").toLowerCase());

  const femaleScore = (dairy ? 0.68 : 0.56)
    + (aspect < 1 ? 0.03 : 0)
    + (stats.dark_ratio > 0.35 ? 0.02 : 0);
  const female = femaleScore >= 0.5;
  const genderConfidence = Math.round(Math.min(0.78, Math.abs(femaleScore - 0.5) * 2 * 0.4 + 0.52) * 100);

  let ageKey = "adult";
  let ageConfidence = 62;
  if (stats.dark_ratio < 0.18 && stats.mean_luma > 0.58) {
    ageKey = "calf";
    ageConfidence = 61;
  } else if (stats.dark_ratio < 0.32 || stats.green_ratio > 0.22) {
    ageKey = "young";
    ageConfidence = 59;
  }

  return {
    gender: {
      key: female ? "female" : "male",
      label: female ? "Female" : "Male",
      confidence: genderConfidence,
      method: "on-device morphology + breed prior",
    },
    age_group: {
      key: ageKey,
      label: AGE_OPTIONS.find((item) => item.key === ageKey)?.label || ageKey,
      confidence: ageConfidence,
      method: "on-device body-size / coat prior",
    },
    stats,
  };
}

export async function runOnDeviceInference({
  canvas,
  model,
  settings,
  oodProfile = null,
  imageMeta = {},
}) {
  const record = model || (await getModel(settings?.activeModel || DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME));
  if (!record) {
    throw new Error("No on-device model selected. Open Settings and upload an ONNX model.");
  }
  if (record.metadata?.runnable === false) {
    throw new Error(record.metadata?.reason || "This checkpoint is not runnable on-device. Export it to ONNX first.");
  }
  const session = await getSession(record);
  const normalizationBaked = inferNormalizationBaked(record.name, record.metadata || {});
  const inputName = session.inputNames?.[0] || "input";
  const tensorDataArray = preprocessToTensor(canvas, normalizationBaked);
  const input = new ort.Tensor("float32", tensorDataArray, [1, 3, IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE]);

  const started = performance.now();
  const outputs = await session.run({ [inputName]: input });
  const { binary, cattle, buffalo } = resolveOutputs(session, outputs);
  const binaryLogits = tensorData(binary);
  const cattleLogits = tensorData(cattle);
  const buffaloLogits = tensorData(buffalo);
  if (!binaryLogits || !cattleLogits || !buffaloLogits) {
    throw new Error("Model outputs are missing binary/cattle/buffalo heads.");
  }
  const latencyMs = performance.now() - started;

  const binaryProbs = softmax(binaryLogits);
  const cattleProbs = softmax(cattleLogits);
  const buffaloProbs = softmax(buffaloLogits);
  const cattleClasses = classListFromModel(record, "cattleClasses", EXPECTED_CATTLE_BREEDS);
  const buffaloClasses = classListFromModel(record, "buffaloClasses", EXPECTED_BUFFALO_BREEDS);

  const combined = [
    ...cattleProbs.map((p) => binaryProbs[0] * p),
    ...buffaloProbs.map((p) => binaryProbs[1] * p),
  ];
  const ranked = combined
    .map((prob, index) => ({ prob, index }))
    .sort((a, b) => b.prob - a.prob)
    .slice(0, 5)
    .map(({ prob, index }) => {
      const isCattle = index < cattleClasses.length;
      const slug = isCattle ? cattleClasses[index] : buffaloClasses[index - cattleClasses.length];
      return {
        breed: breedDisplayName(slug || "unknown"),
        breed_slug: slug || "unknown",
        species: isCattle ? "Cattle" : "Buffalo",
        confidence: Math.round(prob * 10000) / 100,
        prob,
      };
    });

  const top = ranked[0] || { breed: "Unknown", breed_slug: null, species: "Cattle", confidence: 0, prob: 0 };
  const speciesIndex = binaryProbs[1] > binaryProbs[0] ? 1 : 0;
  const species = speciesIndex === 1 ? "Buffalo" : "Cattle";
  const speciesConfidence = Math.round(binaryProbs[speciesIndex] * 10000) / 100;

  const activeLogits = speciesIndex === 1 ? buffaloLogits : cattleLogits;
  const activeProbs = speciesIndex === 1 ? buffaloProbs : cattleProbs;
  const embeddedOod = record.metadata?.ood && typeof record.metadata.ood === "object"
    ? record.metadata.ood
    : null;
  const activeOod = embeddedOod || oodProfile?.json_data || null;
  const temperature = Number(
    activeOod?.energy_temperature ?? settings?.energyTemperature ?? DEFAULT_OOD.energyTemperature
  ) || 1;
  const energyThreshold = Number(
    activeOod?.energy_threshold ?? settings?.energyThreshold ?? DEFAULT_OOD.energyThreshold
  );
  const mspThreshold = Number(
    activeOod?.msp_threshold ?? settings?.mspThreshold ?? DEFAULT_OOD.mspThreshold
  );
  const binaryFloor = Number(
    activeOod?.binary_confidence_floor
      ?? settings?.binaryConfidenceFloor
      ?? DEFAULT_OOD.binaryConfidenceFloor
  );
  const energy = -temperature * logSumExp(activeLogits.map((v) => v / temperature));
  const msp = Math.max(...activeProbs);
  const binaryConfidence = Math.max(...binaryProbs);
  const hasCalibration = Boolean(embeddedOod || oodProfile)
    || record.metadata?.source === "bundled";
  const requiresCalibration = !hasCalibration && record.metadata?.source === "uploaded";
  const embeddedDisabled = embeddedOod?.enabled === false;
  const oodEnabled = settings?.oodEnabled !== false
    && settings?.activeOodProfile !== "disabled"
    && !embeddedDisabled
    && !requiresCalibration;
  const oodByFloor = binaryConfidence < binaryFloor;
  const oodByEnergy = energy > energyThreshold;
  const oodByMsp = msp < mspThreshold;
  const isOod = Boolean(oodEnabled && (oodByFloor || oodByEnergy || oodByMsp));

  const attrs = estimateGenderAge({ breedSlug: top.breed_slug, canvas, imageMeta });

  return {
    model_name: record.name,
    model_source: record.metadata?.source || "uploaded",
    normalization_baked: normalizationBaked,
    species,
    predicted_species: species,
    species_confidence: speciesConfidence,
    species_prob: Math.max(...binaryProbs),
    breed: top.breed,
    top_breed: top.breed,
    breed_slug: top.breed_slug,
    confidence: top.confidence,
    top_breed_confidence: top.confidence,
    top5_breeds: ranked,
    gender: attrs.gender,
    age_group: attrs.age_group,
    is_ood: isOod,
    ood: isOod,
    ood_score: Number(energy.toFixed(4)),
    ood_details: {
      energy: Number(energy.toFixed(4)),
      energy_threshold: energyThreshold,
      msp: Number(msp.toFixed(4)),
      msp_threshold: mspThreshold,
      binary_confidence: Number(binaryConfidence.toFixed(4)),
      binary_confidence_floor: binaryFloor,
      ood_by_energy: oodByEnergy,
      ood_by_msp: oodByMsp,
      ood_by_binary_floor: oodByFloor,
      temperature,
      profile: embeddedOod ? "embedded" : (oodProfile?.filename || settings?.activeOodProfile || "auto"),
      ood_source: embeddedOod ? "embedded" : (oodProfile?.filename ? "profile" : "defaults"),
      requires_calibration: requiresCalibration,
    },
    inference_time_ms: Math.round(latencyMs * 10) / 10,
    total_time_ms: Math.round((performance.now() - started) * 10) / 10,
    routing: "on-device soft routing",
    image_stats: attrs.stats,
  };
}
