function drawPrepared(image, cropMode, base) {
  const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
  canvas.width = base;
  canvas.height = base;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d", { willReadFrequently: true });
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = true;
  ctx.imageSmoothingQuality = "high";

  const w = image.naturalWidth || image.width;
  const h = image.naturalHeight || image.height;
  if (!w || !h) throw new Error("Image has no dimensions.");

  if (cropMode === "pad") {
    const scale = base / Math.max(w, h);
    const dw = Math.max(1, Math.round(w * scale));
    const dh = Math.max(1, Math.round(h * scale));
    ctx.fillStyle = PAD_FILL;
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, base, base);
    ctx.drawImage(image, Math.round((base - dw) / 2), Math.round((base - dh) / 2), dw, dh);
  } else {

    const scale = base / Math.min(w, h);
    const dw = Math.max(1, Math.round(w * scale));
    const dh = Math.max(1, Math.round(h * scale));
    ctx.drawImage(image, Math.round((base - dw) / 2), Math.round((base - dh) / 2), dw, dh);
  }
  return canvas;
}

export async function prepareImage(file, {
  cropMode = "pad",
  scaleMode = "auto",
  manualCropFile = null,
} = {}) {
  const sourceFile = manualCropFile || file;
  const loaded = await loadImageFile(sourceFile);
  try {
    const base = scaleMode === "train" ? TRAIN_RESIZE : IMAGE_SIZE;
    const effectiveCrop = manualCropFile ? "center" : cropMode;
    const baseCanvas = drawPrepared(loaded.image, effectiveCrop, base);
    const canvas = centerCrop260(baseCanvas);
    const blob = await canvasToBlob(canvas);
    const preparedFile = new File(
      [blob],
      `prepared_${Date.now()}.jpg`,
      { type: "image/jpeg", lastModified: Date.now() },
    );
    return {
      file: preparedFile,
      dataUrl: canvasToDataUrl(canvas),
      canvas,
      meta: {
        cropMode: effectiveCrop,
        scaleMode,
        baseSize: base,
        originalWidth: loaded.width,
        originalHeight: loaded.height,
        originalAspect: loaded.width / Math.max(1, loaded.height),
        outputWidth: IMAGE_SIZE,
        outputHeight: IMAGE_SIZE,
        source: "upload",
      },
    };
  } finally {
    loaded.release?.();
  }
}

docs.title: Split Strategy
docs.text:
• Full training: 70/15/15 stratified per (species, breed) with long-tail minimums (≥1 val and ≥1 test image for every breed with ≥3 images)
  • Smoke test: 5 images/breed → 60/20/20 split (tiny but real)

docs.title: Augmentation (OFF by default — opt-in per run)
docs.text:
• Train (no flags): Resize(260) → CenterCrop(260) → ToTensor() — identical to eval
  • Train (opt-in): Resize(288) → RandomResizedCrop(260, scale=0.8-1.0) → RandomHorizontalFlip → ColorJitter(0.2,0.2,0.2,0.1) → RandAugment(ops=2, mag=5) → ToTensor(), gated by --rrc / --flip / --color-jitter / --randaugment (or --augment-all)
  • Eval: Resize(260) → CenterCrop(260) → ToTensor() (EVAL_MATCH_TRAIN_RESOLUTION=True switches to Resize(288)+CenterCrop(260))
  • Batch mixing (opt-in, --mix): 25% chance of CutMix(α=0.4) or MixUp(α=0.2) on the GPU, pairing partners within the same species; disabled for the last 15% of phase 2.

docs.title: Performance Optimizations
docs.text:
• Byte Caching: CACHE_IMAGES stores raw JPEG bytes in RAM instead of decoded PIL.Image objects. This prevents RAM Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors while bypassing slow disk I/O after the first epoch.
  • GPU-Accelerated MixUp/CutMix: Tensor slicing for data mixing is offloaded to the CUDA device in run_epoch, preventing the CPU DataLoader from becoming a bottleneck on platforms like Colab.

docs.title: Label Encoding
docs.text:
• Binary: one-hot [cattle=0, buffalo=1]
  • Breed: one-hot over species-specific classes
  • Masks: cattle_mask=1.0 if cattle, else buffalo_mask=1.0

docs.title: Export & Deployment
docs.text: The classifier exports to desktop testing formats and mobile deployment formats for two Android runtimes (TFLite and ONNX Runtime Mobile). local_train.py exports automatically after training; manual export is fully supported.

docs.title: Export Command
docs.text:
python -m src.export [OPTIONS]
Flag Type Default Description --backbone lite2 | lite4 lite2 Which backbone's checkpoint to export --mode onnx | onnx-int8 | tflite | float16 | portable required Export format --checkpoint path auto (outputs/checkpoints/<backbone>_phase2_best_<runid>.pt) Specific .pt file to use --calibration-images int 500 Train-split images used for INT8 calibration --skip-app-assets flag off Don't copy TFLite artifacts into flutter_app/assets/models/ --onnx-static-batch flag off Fix batch size 1 in the fp32 ONNX export

docs.title: Export Formats
docs.text: Mode Output Use Case portable outputs/export/portable/<backbone>_<tag>/ Python inference with full metadata (test_model.py) onnx outputs/export/<backbone>_fp32.onnx Framework-free desktop testing; caller normalizes input tflite <backbone>_fp32.tflite + <backbone>_int8.tflite + labels_*.txt Flutter app (tflite_flutter) — full-integer INT8 PTQ onnx-int8 <backbone>_mobile_int8.onnx + labels_*.txt ONNX Runtime Mobile — QDQ static INT8 float16 outputs/export/<backbone>_float16.pt FP16 TorchScript

docs.title: Input conventions (important!)
docs.text:
Artifact Input the caller must provide onnx (fp32) ImageNet-normalized tensor (mean/std applied by the caller) — matches test_model.py tflite / onnx-int8 (mobile) RGB float32 in [0, 1] — ImageNet normalization is baked into the graph as constants

The mobile convention means the Flutter engine's existing pixel / 255.0 preprocessing is exactly correct with zero app changes.

docs.title: Portable Bundle
docs.text:
The portable format is a self-contained folder for Python-based inference:

outputs/export/portable/<backbone>_<...>_<runid>/
├── model.pt             # checkpoint containing state_dict + model_meta
├── cattle_classes.json  # optional duplicate of the embedded map
├── buffalo_classes.json # optional duplicate of the embedded map
├── ood_thresholds.json  # optional duplicate of the embedded OOD config
└── model_info.json      # human-readable summary (backbone, image_size, usage)

Self-describing: model.pt now embeds class maps, input resolution, normalization mode and OOD thresholds in ckpt["model_meta"]. The JSON files are kept for compatibility but are not required. Load with src.model_introspect.inspect_and_load_pt().

Note: Portable bundles save state_dict (not TorchScript). Loading requires the BreedClassifier class from src/model.py. For framework-free deployment use ONNX / TFLite instead.

docs.title: TFLite (full-integer INT8)
docs.text:
--mode tflite runs the chain PyTorch → ONNX (static batch 1) → onnx2tf → TFLite FP32 → full-integer INT8 PTQ: - Calibrated on up to 500 real train-split images (--calibration-images) - Per-channel weight quantization, INT8 activations; quantize/dequantize ops at the I/O boundary keep inputs as float32 [0,1] - Emits labels_binary.txt / labels_cattle.txt / labels_buffalo.txt (line i = class i) - Copies model.tflite + labels into flutter_app/assets/models/ automatically (disable with --skip-app-assets) - A TFLite FP32 fallback is emitted alongside for A/B checks

Requires the optional toolchain (see requirements.txt): 

pip install tensorflow onnx2tf tf-keras onnx-graphsurgeon sng4onnx onnxsim

docs.title: ONNX INT8 (ONNX Runtime Mobile)
docs.text: --mode onnx-int8 produces a QDQ static-quantized ONNX model: per-channel weights, INT8 activations, calibrated on the same real train images. Runs with onnxruntime (already a dependency) — no extra toolchain needed.

docs.title: Legacy --mode int8 (removed)
docs.text: The old x86 PTQ path was removed: it failed conversion (Unsupported qscheme: per_channel_affine) and its artifacts were not usable on Android. Running --mode int8 prints this guidance.

docs.title: Manual Export Commands
docs.text:
# Mobile: TFLite INT8 + labels, ready for the Flutter app
python -m src.export --mode tflite --backbone lite2

# Mobile: ONNX Runtime Mobile INT8
python -m src.export --mode onnx-int8 --backbone lite2

# Desktop testing formats
python -m src.export --mode portable  --backbone lite2
python -m src.export --mode onnx      --backbone lite2
python -m src.export --mode float16   --backbone lite2

# Export from a specific checkpoint
python -m src.export --mode tflite --backbone lite2 \
  --checkpoint outputs/checkpoints/lite2_phase2_best_<runid>.pt

docs.title: Parity Gate (always run after exporting)
docs.text:
src.parity_check verifies that the quantized artifacts match the fp32 PyTorch reference before you ship:

# Accuracy mode — same metrics as training validation, per runtime
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 \
  --tflite outputs/export/lite2_int8.tflite \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx \
  --onnx outputs/export/lite2_fp32.onnx \
  --split val

# Artifact-only mode — no dataset needed, random-input logit comparison
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 --synthetic 16 \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx

Acceptance: any INT8 artifact must stay within 1 pt combined_top1 of the fp32 reference. If it fails, fall back to the FP32 TFLite file or revisit calibration. Reports are saved to outputs/metrics/<backbone>_parity*.json.

docs.title: Model Sizes (measured, lite2)
docs.text: Artifact Size Portable model.pt (FP32 state_dict) ~26 MB ONNX FP32 ~25.7 MB ONNX INT8 (QDQ, mobile) ~7.1 MB TFLite INT8 ~6–7 MB (expected)

docs.title: Mobile INT8 pipeline (recommended)
docs.text:
The Android path is converter-side PTQ, not PyTorch QAT:

# 1. Train (2 phases by default; QAT is opt-in and not needed for mobile INT8)
python -m src.train --backbone lite2 --teacher outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt

# 2. Export both runtimes
python -m src.export --mode tflite --backbone lite2
python -m src.export --mode onnx-int8 --backbone lite2

# 3. Parity gate
python -m src.parity_check --backbone lite2 \
  --tflite outputs/export/lite2_int8.tflite \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx

Step 2 places the artifacts the Flutter app expects (tflite_flutter loads assets/models/model.tflite + labels_*.txt), with the input convention the app already uses (pixel / 255.0, outputs read by index: 0=binary, 1=cattle, 2=buffalo).

docs.title: Deployment Options
docs.text: Format File Runtime TFLite INT8 <backbone>_int8.tflite → assets/models/model.tflite tflite_flutter (CPU XNNPACK / GPU delegate) ONNX INT8 <backbone>_mobile_int8.onnx ONNX Runtime Mobile (onnxruntime-android) TFLite FP32 <backbone>_fp32.tflite Fallback if INT8 parity fails

docs.title: QAT (optional recovery path)
docs.text: python -m src.train --include-qat (OFF by default) fine-tunes with fake-quantization and saves a timestamped <backbone>_quantized_<runid>.pt. This is an x86-side recovery tool if converter PTQ drops more than ~2 pts — the artifact is not a TFLite/ORT model.

docs.title: Pre-Inference Image Quality Gate & OOD Explainer
docs.text:
Field photos fail in predictable ways — motion blur, dark barns, blown-out sunlight, tiny uploads, extreme panoramas — and a dropped pixel or two is often all a farmer needs to know to retake the shot. src/image_quality.py detects these conditions before the model runs, in a few milliseconds, with no model, no GPU and no extra dependencies (Pillow + NumPy).

It also converts the OOD detector's three technical thresholds into one plain sentence the farmer can act on, in English, Tamil and Hindi.

docs.title: What is measured
docs.text:
Analysis happens on a grayscale thumbnail (long side 256 px), which makes the metrics resolution-independent and cheap.

Check Metric Flag Sharpness Variance of a 4-neighbour Laplacian is_blurry when < QUALITY_BLUR_THRESHOLD (45) Exposure Mean luminance + shadow/highlight clipping lighting_issue = "too_dark" (mean < 40) or "overexposed" (mean > 225) Resolution Smaller original dimension resolution_issue when < 180 px Framing Long:short side ratio (EXIF orientation respected) aspect_issue when > 2.5 Clipping Fraction of pixels in the darkest/brightest buckets clipping_issue at >= 55%

Thresholds live in src/config.py (QUALITY_*) so they can be tuned against a real validation set without touching code.

Calibration note. On the 256 px thumbnail, sharp scenes measure ~50–170 lap-var; Gaussian blur r=2 ≈ 85, r=3 ≈ 44, r=6 ≈ 7. The 45 threshold catches visible motion blur while letting low-texture backgrounds (dry grass, plain sky) through.

The gate is advisory, not a blocker: a blurry photo still receives a best-effort prediction plus the tips, because a farmer in a field is better served by an answer and a retake suggestion than by an error page. UIs can choose to require action == "proceed" before submitting.

Measured latency: 3.6 ms from JPEG bytes (includes decode) and 1.8 ms when the already-decoded image is reused — well inside the 15 ms budget.

docs.title: OOD explainer
docs.text:
explain_ood_for_user(is_ood, ood_details, quality_report) maps the detector's three thresholds onto two farmer-facing failure modes:

Condition code English message msp < binary_confidence_floor not_animal "No cow or buffalo clearly detected in this photo. Please upload a clear side-view photo of cattle or buffalo." energy > energy_threshold or msp < msp_threshold unclear_features "Animal detected, but breed features (horns, hump, coat) are partially hidden or unclear. Try capturing the full side profile from head to tail." not OOD, quality issues poor_quality "The prediction below is the best available, but the photo quality limits accuracy…" not OOD, clean photo ok "The photo is sharp enough and well exposed for breed analysis."

Every message is trilingual. Raw energy, msp and thresholds are kept under technical for developer views only — they never appear in the headline. Quality tips are merged into the OOD tips and de-duplicated, so the farmer gets one actionable list.

docs.title: API integration
docs.text:
Both prediction services call the gate after decoding and attach two keys:

...

result["quality"] = quality
result["ood_explanation"] = ood_explanation
  • server/services/inference.py → Flask POST /api/predict
  • test_model.py :: ModelManager.predict() → standalone tester + its /api/predict

The rest of the response is unchanged; existing clients can ignore the new keys. The React app renders them in the Advanced drawer (PhotoGuidance), and the main result card now uses the friendly OOD message instead of the generic one.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Blur is a global heuristic: a sharp animal against a defocused background can score lower than expected. The cost of a false positive is a tip, not a blocked prediction.
  • Very low-contrast (dull light) photos naturally measure low lap-var and may report both blurry and too_dark; the lighting tip is the more useful one.
  • Thresholds were calibrated on synthetic scenes and should be spot-checked against a sample of real field photos before tightening the gate.
  • Exposure/brightness uses the whole frame, so a bright sky can mask a dark animal; the metric is deliberately simple and fast.

docs.title: 4-Layer Input Guardrails
docs.text:
A fully offline, no-retraining safety layer that runs before/after the breed classifier. It rejects drawings, screenshots, selfies, other animals and unrelated scenes, and returns a specific trilingual explanation instead of a generic "out of distribution" banner.

Implementation: src/input_guardrails.py Config: GUARDRAIL_* in src/config.py

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
Stage Check Rejects when 1 Photorealism / drawing detector >38% of 8×8 pixel blocks are near-flat (std < 1.8), a near-white/black canvas has sharp edges and low saturation, or the 4×4×4 colour histogram is too sparse (entropy < 1.65 or top-3 bins > 75%) 2 Human / selfie / semantic gate a Haar face/profile face covers ≥4% of the image; the extreme skin-tone fallback fires; or CLIP's best category is human / art / other animal / object (or P(valid) < 0.55) 3 Feature + entropy gate soft-routed 68-breed entropy > 0.78; top-1 < 0.08; or the 1280-d feature L2 norm is outside [5, 120] 4 Logit OOD the existing OODDetector energy / MSP / binary-floor check fires

Any stage can reject. Stages 1–2 run before the network, so a cartoon never spends inference time. Stages 3–4 run on the model tensors.

docs.title: Offline behaviour
docs.text:
• OpenCV is optional. If cv2 is missing, the Haar face check is skipped.
  • CLIP is optional. It reuses the process-wide attributes_zeroshot.get_estimator() and never downloads at import time. If weights are not cached/available, the semantic gate is skipped.
  • The skin-tone fallback is deliberately extreme (>0.92 overall and centre) because brown buffalo coats otherwise look "skin-like" when no face/CLIP detector is available.

docs.title: Calibration note
docs.text: The specification's Stage-3 top-1 floor of 0.18 rejects many valid buffalo images on this checkpoint (validation top-1 ≈ 0.35; real images commonly sit at 0.15–0.25). The shipped default is 0.08, which still rejects extreme uncertainty while leaving the energy/MSP stage to handle the rest. Override GUARDRAIL_TOP1_MIN if you retrain a stronger classifier.

docs.title: Rejection codes
docs.text:
reason_code is one of:

Code Meaning cartoon_or_digital_graphic Clip-art, cartoon, screenshot, flat digital graphic sketch_or_line_drawing White/black canvas with line art synthetic_illustration Too few colours / posterised illustration human_or_selfie Face, portrait or selfie other_animal Dog, goat, sheep, horse, bird, etc. unrelated_object Vehicle, building, document, empty scenery uncertain_animal Animal-like but entropy/top-1/feature norm is abnormal out_of_distribution Energy/MSP/binary-floor OOD signal

The API response contains:

"rejection_info": {
  "rejected": true,
  "reason_code": "human_or_selfie",
  "stage": "Stage 2: Human / Semantic Check",
  "title":       { "en": "...", "ta": "...", "hi": "..." },
  "message":     { "en": "...", "ta": "...", "hi": "..." },
  "instruction": { "en": "...", "ta": "...", "hi": "..." }
}

verdict_to_ood_explanation() also populates the legacy ood_explanation shape (code, severity, title, message, tips_by_language) so older UIs keep working.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text: Surface Behaviour server/services/inference.py Stage 1–2 before inference; Stage 3–4 after. Early rejection returns rejection_info, is_ood=true, guardrail, and zero confidence. src/model.py BreedClassifier.predict_guarded(x, pil_img, ...) returns (out, verdict). test_model.py Same pre/post flow; rejections are shown in the OOD banner using the localized title/message. Schema tests can pass guardrails=False. server/app.py /api/health reports guardrail availability; /api/guardrails/status (dev route) reports OpenCV/CLIP state and thresholds. React PhotoGuidance.jsx prefers rejection_info over the legacy OOD copy.

docs.title: Disable / tune
docs.text:
# src/config.py
GUARDRAIL_ENABLED = False          # master switch
GUARDRAIL_CLIP_ENABLED = False     # never try CLIP
GUARDRAIL_TOP1_MIN = 0.08
GUARDRAIL_ENTROPY_MAX = 0.78

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
python -m unittest tests.test_input_guardrails -v

The tests cover sketch/cartoon/solid rejection, real-photo acceptance, trilingual copy, confident-model acceptance, uniform-entropy rejection, logit-OOD rejection and feature-norm outliers.

docs.title: Local Training — Automated Pipeline
docs.text: The local_train.py script is the recommended entry point for local training. It automates every step from environment setup to dataset download, model training, and multi-format export in a single command.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/Bharaths31/ML-CB-B-identifier
cd ML-CB-B-identifier

# 2. Run the pipeline — pick your preferred data mode:

# Fastest local iteration (25% data, ~4× speedup)
python local_train.py --quarter-data

# Good balance of speed and accuracy (50% data)
python local_train.py --half-data

# Full training (all data, highest accuracy)
python local_train.py

# Sanity check — completes in seconds
python local_train.py --smoke-test

That's it. The script handles all remaining steps automatically.

docs.title: What the Script Does
docs.text:
The pipeline runs 8 stages sequentially:

Stage Name Description §0 Prerequisites Checks Python ≥ 3.9, git, pip availability; Windows: checks MSVC build tools §1 Environment Setup Creates .venv, installs training dependencies §2 Kaggle Download Prompts for API credentials if needed, downloads algsoch/breed-cattle-buffalo §3 Unzip & Organize Extracts images into data/raw/cattle/ and data/raw/buffalo/ §4 Verify Architecture Runs src.verify — confirms backbone loading + forward pass shapes §5 Data Validation Validates dataset structure and breed counts §6 Training Runs src.train with VRAM auto-scaling and appropriate flags §7 Export Exports in 4 formats: portable, ONNX, INT8, float16

Each stage prints a §N — banner with ✅/❌ status indicators.

docs.title: Kaggle API Credentials
docs.text:
The script automatically manages Kaggle credentials.

First run — if ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json doesn't exist, you'll be prompted: 

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Kaggle API credentials required             │
│  Get your key at: kaggle.com/settings → API │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Enter your Kaggle username: your_username
Enter your Kaggle API key:  your_api_key_here
Credentials are saved to ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json for future runs.

Subsequent runs — existing credentials are reused automatically.

Manual credential setup:

Windows: 

mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.kaggle
copy kaggle.json %USERPROFILE%\.kaggle\kaggle.json

Linux / macOS: 

mkdir -p ~/.kaggle
cp kaggle.json ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json
chmod 600 ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json

Getting your API key: Go to kaggle.com/settings → API → Create New Token. Copy username and key from the downloaded kaggle.json.

docs.title: Data Modes
docs.text:
The script supports four data modes (mutually exclusive — pick at most one):

Flag Data Used Typical Speed Best For (none) / --full-data 100% of images Slowest Final production training --half-data 50% per breed (seed=42) ~2× faster Good local GPU training --quarter-data 25% per breed (seed=42) ~4× faster Quick local iteration --smoke-test 5 images/breed, 1 epoch Seconds CI / end-to-end sanity check

Key properties of all subset modes: - Deterministic sampling (seed=42) — same images selected every run - Same 70/15/15 stratified split (with long-tail minimums) applied to the sampled subset - Class maps include ALL 75 breeds — model architecture is identical to full training - --smoke-test uses 60/20/20 split (tiny but real training signal)

docs.title: Full Data (Default)
docs.text:
python local_train.py
# or explicitly:
python local_train.py --full-data
Uses every image for every breed. Produces the highest accuracy but takes the longest.

docs.title: Half Data
docs.text:
python local_train.py --half-data
Uses 50% of images per breed. A good balance of speed and accuracy for GPUs with limited VRAM (e.g., RTX 3050 4 GB).

docs.title: Quarter Data
docs.text:
python local_train.py --quarter-data
Uses 25% of images per breed. ~4× faster than full data. Ideal for quick iteration and validation on very constrained local machines.

docs.title: Smoke Test
docs.text:
python local_train.py --smoke-test
Uses 5 images per breed, 1 epoch per phase. Completes in seconds. Use this to verify the entire pipeline works before committing to a long run.

docs.title: Windows Prerequisites
docs.text:
On Windows, the script automatically checks for Visual C++ Build Tools (MSVC), which some Python packages require to compile C extensions.

What it checks: - cl.exe — MSVC compiler in PATH - vswhere.exe — Visual Studio Build Tools installer registry

If missing, a warning is printed with the download link — but the script does not fail. PyTorch installs via pre-built wheels and does not require MSVC.

⚠️  WARNING: Missing Windows build dependencies:
    - cl.exe
    - Visual Studio / Build Tools installer (vswhere not found)

  Fix: Install 'Microsoft C++ Build Tools' (free):
    https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/
  Select workload: 'Desktop development with C++'

docs.title: VRAM Auto-Scaling
docs.text:
The script automatically detects your GPU's available VRAM and adjusts batch_size and grad_accum to maximize utilization while maintaining a constant effective batch size of 128:

python local_train.py --quarter-data

  --tflite outputs/export/lite2_int8.tflite \
  --onnx-int8 outputs/export/lite2_mobile_int8.onnx

docs.title: Idempotent Re-runs
docs.text:
The script is safe to re-run:

  • venv: Reused if .venv/ already exists (deps still installed to ensure nothing is missing)
  • Dataset: If data/raw/cattle/ and data/raw/buffalo/ exist with breed subdirectories, download is skipped
  • Kaggle credentials: If ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json is valid, no prompt appears
  • Zip cleanup: Downloaded zip is removed after extraction to save disk space

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torch' Run without --skip-setup to install dependencies RuntimeError: Kaggle credentials are required Get your API key at kaggle.com/settings → API Dataset not found at data/raw/ Remove --skip-download to auto-download from Kaggle GPU OOM during training Script auto-scales batch size; if still OOMing, try --quarter-data or --smoke-test BackendCompilerFailed: triton (Windows) Auto-handled — torch.compile is disabled on Windows automatically backbone .pth not found The .pth files are included in the repository — ensure your clone is complete

docs.title: BreedClassifier (src/model.py)
docs.text:
class BreedClassifier(nn.Module):
    backbone: EfficientNetLite     # stem → 7 MBConv stages → head(1280ch)
    attention: CBAM | SEBlock      # inserted after stage 3 (88ch lite2 / 112ch lite4)
    avg_pool: AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
    binary_head: Linear(1280→256→2)
    cattle_head: Linear(1280→512) + BN + ReLU + Drop(0.3) + Linear(512→256) + BN + ReLU + Drop(0.2) + Linear(256→57)
    buffalo_head: Linear(1280→512) + BN + ReLU + Drop(0.3) + Linear(512→256) + BN + ReLU + Drop(0.2) + Linear(256→18)
    trait_heads: Parallel linear layers for multiple morphological traits

docs.title: Forward Path
docs.text:
1. forward_features(x): backbone stages 0..3 → CBAM → stages 4..6 → head → pool → flatten
  2. forward(x): features → 4 parallel heads → dict{binary, cattle, buffalo, features, embedding, traits}

docs.title: Freeze/Unfreeze Methods
docs.text:
• freeze_backbone(): freezes backbone + attention
  • freeze_all() / unfreeze_all(): all parameters
  • backbone_eval() / backbone_train(): BatchNorm mode control

docs.title: EfficientNet-Lite (src/efficientnet_lite.py)
docs.text:
• MBConv blocks with relu6 activation (no SE in lite variant)
  • forward_until(x, stage_idx) / forward_from(x, stage_idx): split forward for attention insertion
  • Weight loading: load_backbone_weights() — strict=False, allows missing fc.*

docs.title: Attention (src/cbam.py)
docs.text:
• CBAM: ChannelAttention(avg+max pool → MLP → sigmoid) → SpatialAttention(avg+max concat → conv → sigmoid)
  • SE: AdaptiveAvgPool → FC reduce → ReLU → FC expand → Sigmoid

docs.title: Self-Describing Models (Zero External JSON)
docs.text:
Every .pt and .onnx artifact is now the single source of truth for how to run it. test_model.py and the Flask API no longer need cattle_classes.json, buffalo_classes.json, model_info.json or outputs/ood/*.json beside a model.

Two mechanisms work together:

  1. Runtime introspection — src/model_introspect.py derives the contract from tensors / the ONNX graph, so files exported before this change work immediately.
  2. Embedded metadata — scripts/embed_metadata.py (and src/export.py) permanently writes the contract into the file.

docs.title: 1. Runtime API
docs.text:
from src.model_introspect import inspect_and_load

bundle = inspect_and_load("path/to/model.pt")   # or .onnx
# bundle.engine              -> "pt" | "onnx" | "torchscript"
# bundle.model_or_session    -> nn.Module or onnxruntime.InferenceSession
# bundle.transform           -> torchvision Compose for THIS model
# bundle.cattle_inv_map      -> {0: "amritmahal", ...}
# bundle.buffalo_inv_map     -> {0: "banni", ...}
# bundle.ood_config          -> embedded thresholds (or config defaults)
# bundle.image_size, bundle.normalization_baked, bundle.input_dtype
# bundle.spec_summary()      -> JSON-safe description for the Dev Console

Specialised entry points: inspect_and_load_pt(path, device), inspect_and_load_onnx(path, use_cuda), and describe_model_file(path).

docs.title: What is introspected
docs.text:
Field PyTorch source ONNX source Backbone (lite2/lite4) backbone.blocks.0.0._project_conv.weight width (16 / 24) metadata, else filename fallback Attention (cbam/se) presence of attention.spatial_attention.conv.weight metadata Head widths binary_head.0.weight, cattle_head.0.weight output shapes Class counts final cattle_head.<fi>.weight / buffalo_head.<fi>.weight last dim of cattle / buffalo outputs Cosine head final head weight has no bias metadata Image size metadata, default IMAGE_SIZE input.shape[2] Normalization metadata, default caller-side embedded mean/std initializers, leading Sub → Div, or *mobile* / *int8* filename Class names metadata → EXPECTED_*_BREEDS (count match) → local JSON → synthetic same OOD thresholds ckpt["model_meta"]["ood"] metadata_props["ood"]

Class maps are accepted as {name: idx}, {idx: name}, a list of names, or a JSON string. A map is only used when its length matches the head width, so a 50-class map can never be paired with a 42-class head.

docs.title: Normalization correctness
docs.text:
bundle.transform stops at ToTensor() when normalization_baked=True. Mobile ONNX exports (_MobileOutputs) already contain (x - mean) / std, so this prevents the historical double-normalization bug. Raw ONNX exports (_RawOutputs) and PyTorch checkpoints get Normalize(mean, std) as before.

Inference code should always call bundle.transform(img) instead of a global TRANSFORM.

docs.title: 2. Embedding metadata
docs.text:
# every model under outputs/
python scripts/embed_metadata.py --all

# one or more files
python scripts/embed_metadata.py --file outputs/checkpoints/my_model.pt
python scripts/embed_metadata.py --file outputs/export/my_model.onnx

# inspect without running inference
python scripts/embed_metadata.py --inspect outputs/export/my_model.onnx

# override auto-detection
python scripts/embed_metadata.py --file model.onnx \
  --cattle-classes data/splits/cattle_classes.json \
  --buffalo-classes data/splits/buffalo_classes.json \
  --ood-json outputs/ood/my_model.json \
  --baked-normalization

Behaviour:

  • .pt — adds/updates ckpt["model_meta"] and preserves phase, epoch, metrics, optimizer state, etc. A raw state_dict is wrapped as {"state_dict": ..., "model_meta": ...}. TorchScript archives store the same JSON in an extra file (model_meta.json).
  • .onnx — replaces duplicate keys in metadata_props and writes the contract as JSON strings (idempotent).
  • Files are written atomically; weights are never modified.
  • OOD thresholds are auto-discovered from the model's directory or outputs/ood/; otherwise src/config.py defaults are embedded.

src/export.py calls the embedders automatically for --mode onnx, --mode onnx-int8 (FP32 + INT8), and --mode float16, and the portable bundle's model.pt is embedded too. src/train.py embeds metadata into every saved checkpoint and re-embeds the calibrated OOD thresholds after training.

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text: The model is trained in two sequential phases by default (QAT is opt-in), each with distinct objectives, frozen layers, and hyperparameters. The entire pipeline is orchestrated by src/train.py and invoked automatically by local_train.py.

docs.title: Two-Phase Training (QAT opt-in)
docs.text:
Phase Name Frozen Layers Learning Rate Epochs Loss Weights Phase 1 All-heads warmup Backbone + attention 3e-3 8 bin=0.15, cat=0.5, buf=0.35 Phase 2 Multi-task fine-tune Differential LR (Backbone 0.1x) 2e-4 (warmup + cosine) + EMA 80 bin=0.15→0.05, cat=0.5→0.55, buf=0.35→0.40 Phase 3 QAT (opt-in, --include-qat) Nothing 5e-6 10 bin=0.15, cat=0.5, buf=0.35

Phase 1 trains all three heads (binary, cattle, buffalo) while keeping the backbone frozen. This anchors the new classification layers to the pre-trained feature extractor before full fine-tuning.

Phase 2 unfreezes everything and jointly optimizes the entire network using differential learning rates (backbone 0.1x, attention 0.5x, heads 1.0x). It also employs an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) model to stabilize weights across iterations. The masked loss ensures the cattle head only trains on cattle images, and the buffalo head only on buffalo images. Once binary_acc ≥ 0.95, the loss weights automatically rebalance to 0.05/0.55/0.40.

Phase 3 is opt-in (--include-qat). Android INT8 now comes from converter-side PTQ (src/export --mode tflite / onnx-int8), so QAT is only a recovery tool when converter PTQ drops more than ~2 pts. It uses per-tensor quantization observers (converts cleanly), starts from the best phase-2 EMA checkpoint, and saves a timestamped <backbone>_quantized_<runid>.pt.

docs.title: Knowledge Distillation (--teacher)
docs.text:
Train a bigger teacher once, then distill into the student at zero extra on-device cost — the student keeps the lite2 architecture, size, and latency:

# Step 1 — train the teacher (lite4 + CBAM)
python -m src.train --backbone lite4

# Step 2 — distill into the lite2 student
python -m src.train --backbone lite2 \
  --teacher outputs/checkpoints/lite4_phase2_best_<runid>.pt \
  --teacher-backbone lite4

The distillation loss blends hard-label supervision with teacher soft targets on all three heads (binary, cattle, buffalo):

L = (1 − α) · masked_hard_CE  +  α · T² · masked_KL(teacher ‖ student)

Defaults: KD_ALPHA = 0.7, KD_TEMPERATURE = 4.0 (see src/config.py). The teacher runs frozen (eval mode) on the same augmented batch, so CutMix/MixUp images are distilled too. With an identical teacher the KL term is exactly zero; with --teacher omitted the run is a plain supervised run.

docs.title: EMA (Exponential Moving Average)
docs.text:
Phase 2 maintains an EMA of the weights with EMA_DECAY = 0.999, updated once per optimizer step (not per micro-batch) with warm-up decay_t = min(0.999, (1+t)/(10+t)). At phase start it prints steps/epoch, total optimizer steps and the EMA time constant, warning if it exceeds 25% of phase-2 steps. Validation runs on both the raw and EMA weights each eval; the checkpoint is saved from whichever scores better (blended_score).

Important: the EMA tracks parameters and BatchNorm buffers (running mean/var are EMA'd, num_batches_tracked is hard-copied). Removing the buffer sync produces checkpoints with stale BN statistics that silently degrade both validation accuracy and every model exported from them.

docs.title: SOTA Optimizations
docs.text: Technique Value Effect Optimizer AdamW, weight_decay=1e-2 Decoupled weight decay, better generalization LR schedule Linear warmup (3 epochs) → Cosine annealing Stable Phase 2 convergence Label smoothing ε=0.05 Prevents overconfident predictions Gradient accumulation 2 steps Effective batch=128 even on small GPUs Gradient clipping max_norm=1.0 Prevents gradient explosions EMA decay=0.999, once per optimizer step, warm-up (1+t)/(10+t) (params + BN buffers) Stabilizes validation & checkpoint selection Effective-number sampler SAMPLER_BETA=0.99 Balances rare breeds without over-oversampling 5-image breeds Logit adjustment LOGIT_ADJUST=False (opt-in --logit-adjust) Off by default; sampler is the single long-tail mechanism SupCon features CONTRASTIVE_WEIGHT=0.2 Separates visually near-identical breeds in embedding space Binary species balancing BALANCE_BINARY_HEAD=True Neutralizes the 57:18 breed-count species prior Batch mixing (opt-in) --mix: CutMix(α=0.4) / MixUp(α=0.2), p=0.25, same-species Off by default; disabled for the last 15% of phase 2 Augmentation (opt-in) --flip/--color-jitter/--randaugment/--rrc/--augment-all Off by default; no-aug train transform == eval transform Outputs TIMESTAMP_OUTPUTS=True, RUN_ID_FORMAT=%d-%m-%Y-%H-%M Timestamped, non-overwriting checkpoints/exports Distillation α=0.7, T=4.0 (optional --teacher) Teacher accuracy in the student at zero device cost

docs.title: CUDA Optimizations
docs.text:
Automatically applied when a CUDA device is detected:

  • cudnn.benchmark = True — auto-tunes convolution algorithms for your hardware
  • TF32 enabled for Ampere+ GPUs (A100, RTX 30xx/40xx) — huge speedup, negligible precision loss
  • torch.amp.autocast("cuda") + GradScaler — mixed-precision training (phases 1–2)
  • pin_memory=True on all DataLoaders
  • persistent_workers=True on DataLoaders
  • non_blocking=True on .to(device) transfers
  • optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) — faster than filling with zeros
  • GPU-accelerated CutMix and MixUp (tensor slicing on CUDA, not CPU)
  • torch.compile(model) — compilation enabled on Linux (auto-disabled on Windows)

docs.title: CPU Fallback
docs.text: All CUDA optimizations gracefully skip when running on CPU. AMP scaler is None, cudnn settings are not touched, torch.compile is skipped. CPU training is significantly slower but fully functional.

docs.title: Loss Functions
docs.text:
soft_ce: Soft cross-entropy that supports fractional label vectors from CutMix/MixUp: 

loss = −(target_smooth × log_softmax(pred + τ·log_prior)).sum(dim=1)
where target_smooth = (1 - ε) × target + ε / num_classes
Logit adjustment is OFF by default (LOGIT_ADJUST=False): the effective-number sampler already rebalances every batch, so adding τ·log_prior too double-corrects and over-predicts rare breeds at inference. When enabled with --logit-adjust, the smoothed log class prior (from the effective sampled distribution by default) is added to the logits with weight LOGIT_ADJUST_TAU; the shift is absorbed into the learned biases, so inference stays raw.

masked_loss: Combines three heads with species masking: 

L = w_bin × CE(binary) + w_cat × CE(cattle) × cattle_mask + w_buf × CE(buffalo) × buffalo_mask
    + λ_supcon × SupCon(projection_head(features))
The cattle/buffalo head losses are only computed on images of the corresponding species. This prevents the buffalo head from receiving gradient signal on cattle images and vice versa.

The binary term is additionally species-balanced per batch (BALANCE_BINARY_HEAD=True): because the per-breed sampler leaves a ~57:18 species prior, each species' binary-CE mass is renormalized to 0.5 with adaptive sample weights (this is an identity on perfectly balanced batches).

The auxiliary supervised-contrastive term (CONTRASTIVE_WEIGHT) uses the previously-unused pooled 1280-d features through a projection head; it is skipped on CutMix/MixUp batches where labels are soft. Once binary_acc ≥ BINARY_SATURATION_ACC, the loss weights automatically rebalance from 0.15/0.50/0.35 to 0.05/0.55/0.40 (see LOSS_WEIGHT_*_FINAL).

masked_kd_loss: the distillation blend described above — (1−α)·masked_loss + α·T²·masked_KL, temperature-scaled on all three heads with the same species masking, plus the SupCon term.

Checkpoint selection: BEST_METRIC="blended_score" = 0.5·macro-F1 + 0.5·combined_top1_soft. Pure macro-F1 is too noisy with 1–2 val images per rare breed; pure top-1 is dominated by the ~10 large breeds. Each eval logs both raw and EMA metrics and saves whichever scores better, plus few/medium/many-shot accuracy and predicted-histogram entropy.

docs.title: Smoke Test (--smoke-test)
docs.text: 5 images per breed, 1 epoch per phase. Uses prepare_smoke_splits(): - Samples real images from the full dataset (not artificial batches) - 60/20/20 train/val/test split - Full 75-class map maintained - Runs in seconds — use for CI or pre-training verification

docs.title: Half-Data Mode (--half-data)
docs.text: 50% of images per breed via prepare_half_splits(): - Deterministic sampling (seed=42) — same images every run - Stratified split (70/15/15) with long-tail minimums applied to the sampled subset - Full 75-class map maintained — architecture identical to full training - ~2× faster than full training

docs.title: Quarter-Data Mode (--quarter-data)
docs.text:
25% of images per breed via prepare_quarter_splits(): - Deterministic sampling (seed=42) — same images every run - Stratified split (70/15/15) with long-tail minimums applied to the sampled subset - Full 75-class map maintained — architecture identical to full training - ~4× faster than full training — ideal for resource-constrained local machines

All data modes are mutually exclusive: --smoke-test, --half-data, --quarter-data.

docs.title: Automated Local Pipeline
docs.text:
For a fully automated experience that handles all stages from setup to export:

# Quarter data — fastest local run
python local_train.py --quarter-data

# Half data — balanced
python local_train.py --half-data

# Opt-in QAT phase (recovery tool; mobile INT8 uses converter PTQ)
python local_train.py --include-qat

See Local Training (Automated) for all flags.

docs.title: Auto-Export
docs.text:
After training completes, the pipeline automatically creates a portable export in outputs/export/portable/ containing: - model.pt — PyTorch checkpoint (state_dict) - cattle_classes.json — cattle breed label map - buffalo_classes.json — buffalo breed label map - model_info.json — architecture metadata + usage instructions

local_train.py additionally exports ONNX, INT8, and float16 formats.

docs.title: Verification & Validation (V&V) Suite
docs.text:
A single command exercises the model, API contract, OOD safety, knowledge base, trilingual UI and themes. It prints a PASS/FAIL/WARN scorecard and writes a review-ready markdown report.

python -m tests.run_vv_suite
# partial run (does not overwrite the report)
python -m tests.run_vv_suite --suite "3."
# skip the latency benchmark
python -m tests.run_vv_suite --skip-benchmark

# standalone UI audit used by Suite 5
node breed-classifier-react/src/verify_ui_i18n.mjs

Reports: outputs/metrics/vv_review_report.md and .json (generated, ignored by git).

Download with the project's built-in Kaggle facility (never commit credentials):

$env:KAGGLE_USERNAME="<user>"
$env:KAGGLE_KEY="<token>"
python data_collection.py --source kaggle `
  --dataset atharvadarpude/indian-buffalo-dataset `
  --output data/external/atharvadarpude_buffalo

data/external/ is gitignored. The suite picks the dataset up automatically when present and skips with a WARN otherwise.
